PSY 426.subject: PSY
PSY 426.description: Explores psychological theories and empirical research on gender across historical and contemporary social contexts. Examines how gender is constructed, experienced, and studied in psychology, including the impact of stereotypes and structural inequities in society, healthcare, and psychological research. Investigates the intersection of gender with race and other identities and systems of oppression, as well as strategies for promoting equity and inclusion within psychology, with an emphasis on resilience and liberation.
attributes: Difference/Power/Discrimination; CSDP – Core Ed - Advanced Difference
PSY 426.prerequisites_raw: PSY 202Z with C- or better or PSY 202HZ with C- or better or PSY 202 with C- or better or PSY 202H with C- or better
PSY 426.recommended: Completion of a Difference, Power, and Oppression Foundations course

PSY 427.subject: PSY
PSY 427.description: Introduces psychological theories and concepts pertaining to different racial groups in the United States. Explores historical and contemporary racism in the U.S. and its psychological effect on racial identity and the intersections of race, ethnicity, sex, gender identity, social class, and nationality. Explores racism and intersecting forms of oppression in the discipline of psychology. Develops cultural competence and humility to prepare students to live and work with individuals from diverse socio-cultural backgrounds.
PSY 427.prerequisites_raw: (PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better) and (PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-] or PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-])
PSY 427.recommended: Completion of a Difference, Power, and Oppression Foundations course

PSY 428.subject: PSY
PSY 428.description: Explores a range of legal issues that are informed by behavioral sciences research in general, and psychology in particular. Focuses on areas including but not limited to psychologists and the legal system; lawyers: socialization, training and ethics; morality and justice; forensic assessment; competency and insanity; eyewitness identification; jury selection theories on crime; punishment and sentencing. Considers issues of culture, gender, and age as they pertain to the specific topics.
PSY 428.prerequisites_raw: PSY 360 with C- or better or PSY 360H with C- or better or PSY 370 with C- or better or PSY 381 with C- or better

PSY 432.subject: PSY
PSY 432.description: Basic vertebrate neurophysiology and neuroanatomy in relation to behavior. Neural and hormonal correlates of sensation, learning, memory and motivation.

PSY 433.subject: PSY
PSY 433.description: Drug-brain-behavior interactions. Psychoactive drugs and their relationships to normal and abnormal behavior in humans.
PSY 433.recommended: Upper-division standing and biological science background

PSY 437.subject: PSY
PSY 437.description: Biological, learning, and cognitive approaches to human and animal motivation. Topics include evolution, homeostasis, drive, arousal, incentive motivation, achievement motivation, and social motivation.
PSY 437.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 330 with C- or better or PSY 340 with C- or better or PSY 340H with C- or better) and ( PSY 301 [C-] or PSY 301H [C-])

PSY 440.subject: PSY
PSY 440.description: Advanced scientific methodology primarily in the areas of attention, learning, memory, and thinking. Students will design their own research projects, collect and analyze data, and write a professional report.
attributes: CSWC – Core Ed - Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); CWIC – Bacc Core
PSY 440.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 301 with D- or better or PSY 301H with D- or better) and ( PSY 340 [D-] or PSY 340H [D-])

PSY 442.subject: PSY
PSY 442.description: Fundamental concepts of animal and human sensation and perception, with emphasis on audition and vision. Applications of psychophysical methods to research in all sensory modalities. Includes review workshops on basic mathematical, physical and physiological concepts necessary to interpret research in this field.
PSY 442.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 301 with C- or better or PSY 301H with C- or better) and ( PSY 330 [C-] or PSY 340 [C-] or PSY 340H [C-])

PSY 444.subject: PSY
PSY 444.description: Experimental and theoretical work on learning, conditioning, and memory in animals and humans.
PSY 444.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 301 with C- or better or PSY 301H with C- or better) and ( PSY 340 [C-] or PSY 340H [C-])

PSY 446.subject: PSY
PSY 446.description: Explore biological, behavioral, perceptual, cognitive and social issues relevant to how humans interact with other computing technology from a psychological science perspective. Evaluate, design, and experimentally test human computer interactions using experimental methods in psychological science.
PSY 446.prerequisites_raw: PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better

PSY 448.subject: PSY
PSY 448.description: Psychological, phenomenological, and physiological approaches to the content and processes of subjective awareness. Topics include philosophical issues, cortical and reticular neurophysiology, sleeping and dreaming, selective attention, imagery, and self-awareness.
PSY 448.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 301 with C- or better or PSY 301H with C- or better) and ( PSY 340 [C-] or PSY 340H [C-])

PSY 450.subject: PSY
PSY 450.description: Examines psychological theories of learning applied to educational contexts including behaviorism, information processing, social cognitivism, and constructivism. Emphasizes review of literature in selected topic area and writing a psychological research or program proposal.
PSY 450.prerequisites_raw: PSY 340 with C- or better or PSY 340H with C- or better or PSY 350 with C- or better

PSY 452.subject: PSY
PSY 452.description: Explores meanings of culture. Examines topics in cognitive, social, developmental, and health psychology in light of various cultural backgrounds, orientations, and forces. Emphasizes contemporary applications of empirical findings from cross-cultural psychological research. Develops a historical, ecological, and global perception of psychology.
PSY 452.prerequisites_raw: (PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better) and (PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-] or PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-])

PSY 454.subject: PSY
PSY 454.description: Discusses intellectual development from infancy to adulthood. Topics include the origin of thinking, the development of perception, attention, memory, problem solving, language, academic skills, and social cognition. Piaget, Vygotsky, and information processing approaches will be discussed.

PSY 456.subject: PSY
PSY 456.description: Covers theories and research concerning human social development. Topics include theories of socialization; the development of social relationships; the self-concept; emotion; sex roles; social cognition; pro-social behavior; morality; self-control; and aggression.

PSY 457.subject: PSY
PSY 457.description: Examines autism and neurodiversity from a psychological perspective. Emphasizes the scientific basis of autism and neurodiversity, with an emphasis on research co-created with autistic researchers and reflecting the lived experience of autistic and neurodivergent individuals, including those with a range of support needs, in social context. Critically examines historical and current diagnostic criteria and processes, evidence-based therapies, interventions and supports, and inclusive workplace, educational, legal, and healthcare environments that allow autistic and neurodivergent people to enjoy fulfilling, interdependent lives in community with other neurotypical and neurodivergent people.
PSY 457.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better or PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better) and ( PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-] or PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-])

PSY 458.subject: PSY
PSY 458.description: Psychological processes involved in the acquisition and use of language throughout childhood. Biological, cognitive, and social influences on language will be discussed, as well as personal uses of language, such as language in thought and reading.

PSY 460.subject: PSY
PSY 460.description: Advanced experimental research methods in the social sciences. Issues in psychological construct operationalization, experimental design, data collection, analysis, and report writing will be emphasized.
attributes: CSWC – Core Ed - Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); CWIC – Bacc Core
PSY 460.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 301 with D- or better or PSY 301H with D- or better) and ( PSY 360 [D-] or PSY 360H [D-])

PSY 460H.subject: PSY
PSY 460H.description: Advanced experimental research methods in the social sciences. Issues in psychological construct operationalization, experimental design, data collection, analysis, and report writing will be emphasized.
attributes: CSWC – Core Ed - Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); CWIC – Bacc Core
Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); HNRS – Honors Course Designator
PSY 460H.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 301 with D- or better or PSY 301H with D- or better) and ( PSY 360 [D-] or PSY 360H [D-])

PSY 462.subject: PSY
PSY 462.description: Examines disability from social psychological and disability studies perspectives. Emphasizes the social construction of disability and its inter- and intra-personal ramifications. Explores stereotyping, prejudice and discrimination, adaptation to disability, disability identity, working with people with disabilities, intersectionality, and sexuality.
PSY 462.prerequisites_raw: PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better or PSY 202 with C- or better or PSY 202H with C- or better or PSY 202Z with C- or better or PSY 202HZ with C- or better
PSY 462.recommended: Completion of a Difference, Power, and Oppression Foundations course

PSY 463.subject: PSY
PSY 463.description: Explores ways to improve judgment and decision making through the application of research from cognitive psychology. Emphasis on development of critical thinking skills.
PSY 463.prerequisites_raw: PSY 340 with C- or better or PSY 340H with C- or better

PSY 464.subject: PSY
PSY 464.description: Research and theory concerning cognitive structures and processes underlying social judgment and social behavior. Topics include attribution theory, social inference, person memory, schema-based information processing.
PSY 464.prerequisites_raw: PSY 360 with C- or better or PSY 360H with C- or better

PSY 467.subject: PSY
PSY 467.description: Survey of classic and contemporary perspectives in political psychology. Special focus on how citizens form political judgments. Topics include personality, affect, cognition, group influence, voting, nationalism, and political tolerance.
PSY 467.prerequisites_raw: PSY 360 with C- or better or PSY 360H with C- or better

PSY 468.subject: PSY
PSY 468.description: Explores the research and theory on the development, maintenance, and dissolution of human relationships. Examines various directions to the study of interpersonal relationships, including attachment, evolutionary-biological, cognition, and interdependence. Topics include physical attraction, love, friendship, communication, trust, jealousy, and several issues that are specific to troubled dyadic relations.
PSY 468.prerequisites_raw: PSY 360 with C- or better or PSY 360H with C- or better

PSY 476.subject: PSY
PSY 476.description: Examines empirical findings, phenomena, and theories related to nonverbal behavior and its perception from a psychological perspective. Covers topics including: theories of nonverbal behavior encoding, decoding, and their accuracy; the neurophysiological basis for nonverbal behavior; valid assessments of nonverbal behavior abilities; and the impact that nonverbal behavior has on interaction processes and social relationships.
PSY 476.prerequisites_raw: PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better or PSY 202 with C- or better or PSY 202H with C- or better or PSY 202Z with C- or better or PSY 202HZ with C- or better

PSY 478.subject: PSY
PSY 478.description: Explores the physiological and psychological factors that play a role in the development of stress, along with subsequent coping strategies that can be used to regulate stress and enhance psychological well-being. Examines how multiple factors, including social, personality, developmental, cognitive, and biological processes, impact stress and coping in a variety of life domains.
PSY 478.prerequisites_raw: (( PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better) and ( PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-])) or ((PSY 201 [C-] or PSY 201H [C-]) and (PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-]))

PSY 480.subject: PSY
PSY 480.description: Advanced research methods used in clinical psychology research. Design of studies, assessment, data collection, and interpretation will be discussed. The clinical content area focused on will vary.
attributes: CSWC – Core Ed - Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); CWIC – Bacc Core
PSY 480.prerequisites_raw: ( PSY 301 with D- or better or PSY 301H with D- or better) and PSY 381 [D-]

PSY 482.subject: PSY
PSY 482.description: Survey of the theory, techniques and research on the major contemporary systems of psychotherapy.
PSY 482.prerequisites_raw: PSY 370 with C- or better or PSY 380 with C- or better or PSY 381 with C- or better or PSY 481 with C- or better

PSY 483.subject: PSY
PSY 483.description: Developmental perspective on child and adolescent psychological disorders including causal factors, associated features, and research-supported interventions.
PSY 483.prerequisites_raw: PSY 350 with C- or better or PSY 381 with C- or better or PSY 481 with C- or better

PSY 484.subject: PSY
PSY 484.description: Focuses on the psychological factors in drug and behavioral addictions and associated interventions. The approach will be biopsychosocial, addressing neurobiological, behavioral, psychological, and social factors that influence addiction. Topics will include epidemiology and public health impact, diagnosis, models of addiction, and intervention and treatment approaches.
attributes: CSWC – Core Ed - Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); CWIC – Bacc Core
PSY 484.prerequisites_raw: H 220 with C- or better or PSY 301 with C- or better or PSY 301H with C- or better or SOC 315 with C- or better

PSY 485.subject: PSY
PSY 485.description: Review of basics of operant and classical conditioning. Research on behavior modification and behavior therapy with both normal and abnormal animals, human adults, and children. Application areas include behavior problems, handicaps, eating disorders, time management, self-control stress management, contingency contracts, and cognitive therapies.
PSY 485.prerequisites_raw: PSY 350 with C- or better or PSY 380 with C- or better or PSY 381 with C- or better or PSY 481 with C- or better
PSY 485.recommended: Background work in family life or education

PSY 486.subject: PSY
PSY 486.description: Examines the use of yoga in psychological practice with a particular focus on managing mental and physical illnesses.
PSY 486.prerequisites_raw: (PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better) and (PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-] or PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-])

PSY 488.subject: PSY
PSY 488.description: Focuses on the psychological science of humans' reactions to traumatic events. Critically examines the social and cultural context for those events and reactions, including systemic racism, sexism, and other forms of oppression. Explores the psychological science of healing, resilience, and liberation, in the context of evidence-based clinical psychological treatments, institutional courage, and societal change.
PSY 488.prerequisites_raw: (PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better) and (PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-] or PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-])
PSY 488.recommended: Completion of a Difference, Power, and Oppression Foundations course

PSY 492.subject: PSY
PSY 492.description: Explores connections between the study of human behavior and the achievement of conservation goals. Understanding how people think about and interact with nature is crucial for promoting environmental sustainability and human well-being. Students will examine theory and research on human cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses to nature.
PSY 492.prerequisites_raw: (PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better) and (PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-] or PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-])

PSY 492H.subject: PSY
PSY 492H.description: Explores connections between the study of human behavior and the achievement of conservation goals. Understanding how people think about and interact with nature is crucial for promoting environmental sustainability and human well-being. Students will examine theory and research on human cognitive, emotional, and behavioral responses to nature.
PSY 492H.prerequisites_raw: (PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better) and (PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-] or PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-])

PSY 493.subject: PSY
PSY 493.description: Psychological theory, research, and interventions directed at how humans can flourish and identify and enhance positive strengths. Topics include positive emotional and cognitive states and processes, prosocial behavior, positive school and work environments, and discovering meaning in life.
PSY 493.prerequisites_raw: PSY 360 with C- or better or PSY 360H with C- or better or PSY 370 with C- or better

PSY 494.subject: PSY
PSY 494.description: Survey human capabilities and limitations in human-machine interaction, including vision, memory, attention, motor control, and human error. Emphasis on theory and implications for system designs.
PSY 494.prerequisites_raw: PSY 340 with C- or better or PSY 340H with C- or better

PSY 495.subject: PSY
PSY 495.description: Explores the psychological processes of meditation, and requires regular meditation sessions by students. Readings ranging from traditional Eastern philosophy to empirical psychological research journal articles will focus on outcomes and effective methods of meditation practice.
PSY 495.prerequisites_raw: (PSY 201 with C- or better or PSY 201H with C- or better or PSY 201Z with C- or better or PSY 201HZ with C- or better) and (PSY 202 [C-] or PSY 202H [C-] or PSY 202Z [C-] or PSY 202HZ [C-])

PSY 496.subject: PSY
PSY 496.description: Survey of psychological research and theory relevant to organizations, industry, and other work settings. Topics include training, employee selection, performance evaluation, work attitudes, and motivation.
PSY 496.prerequisites_raw: PSY 360 with C- or better or PSY 360H with C- or better or PSY 370 with C- or better

PSY 498.subject: PSY
PSY 498.description: Psychological factors in the maintenance of good health and in the prevention of, treatment of, and recovery from illness: Behavioral contributions to illness, life-style risk factors, stress and the immune system, psychological response to symptoms and care-givers, health habits and self-care, management of pain and chronic illness, disability and terminal illness.
PSY 498.prerequisites_raw: PSY 330 with C- or better or PSY 340 with C- or better or PSY 340H with C- or better or PSY 350 with C- or better or PSY 360 with C- or better or PSY 360H with C- or better or PSY 370 with C- or better or PSY 381 with C- or better or PSY 481 with C- or better

PSY 514.subject: PSY
PSY 514.description: An introduction to the tools and methods that psychologists use to examine the processes that underlie human behavior. Emphasis is on the skills necessary for completing a research study: hypothesis formulation, design criteria, data collection, analysis, interpretation, write-up, and presentation of results. Utilizes a combination of readings, discussions, and class exercises. Course culminates in an independent research project proposal.

PSY 515.subject: PSY
PSY 515.course_name: METHODS AND ETHICS FOR CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGISTS
PSY 515.description: Introduces ethical, legal, and professional issues associated with the practice of clinical psychology, as well as the theoretical and research bases of ethical clinical psychological practice. Through hands-on practice with evidence-based psychotherapy skills, examines basics of ethical, effective, culturally-, disability-, gender-affirming psychotherapy. Reviews ethics codes, including the American Psychological Association’s ethics code, as well as policies and laws regarding the practice of clinical psychology.

PSY 516.subject: PSY
PSY 516.course_name: CLASSIFICATION, DIAGNOSIS, AND VARIATION IN CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY
PSY 516.description: Examines the theoretical and scientific basis of prominent categorical, dimensional, and transdiagnostic approaches to the classification and diagnosis of psychopathology. Evaluates research design, methods, and ethics that underlie the empirical basis of effective classification and evaluation of interventions. Explores the theoretical and empirical bases for understanding psychological functioning in the context of human variation and diversity, including culturally-, disability-, and gender-affirming approaches.

PSY 517.subject: PSY
PSY 517.course_name: THEORY AND PRACTICE OF ASSESSMENT IN CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY
PSY 517.description: Reviews select clinical assessment methodologies focusing on skill development in conducting evaluations, synthesizing data, and crafting effective psychological reports. Emphasizes critical analysis of assessment techniques and iterative refinement of reporting skills to enhance clarity and effectiveness. Trains students to provide and apply constructive feedback to improve assessment strategies and reports.

PSY 518.subject: PSY
PSY 518.course_name: THEORY AND PRACTICE OF INTERVENTIONS IN CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY
PSY 518.description: Explores the application of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), combining theoretical foundations with practical implementation across diverse clinical settings. Focuses on the critical evaluation of interventions through theoretical, empirical, and client-centered lenses. Prioritizes skill enhancement in CBT techniques through continuous practice, providing and applying feedback, and alignment with current research and clinical best practices.

PSY 519.subject: PSY
PSY 519.course_name: THEORY AND PRACTICE OF SUPERVISION IN CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGY
PSY 519.description: Explores the application of best practices of clinical supervision in psychology, combining theoretical and research foundations with practical implementation. Prioritizes skill enhancement in providing supervision to clinical psychology trainees, through continuous practice, providing and applying feedback, and alignment with current research and clinical best practices.

PSY 521.subject: PSY
PSY 521.description: Professional development seminar focused on professional issues specific to the field of research-based psychology. Includes writing for publication, professional speaking, professional development and leadership, and current professional and research controversies. Each iteration of the course over the academic year will have a different focus.

PSY 523.subject: PSY
PSY 523.description: Covers research ethics in psychology. Topics include the history of research-oriented ethical guidelines, ethical principles, working with an IRB, questionable research practices, and fraud. Meets OSU’s Learning Outcome regarding the ethical conduct of research.
PSY 523.recommended: An undergraduate-level psychological research methods course

PSY 526.subject: PSY
PSY 526.description: Survey of theories, life cycles and contemporary problems of women and men in a social context. Scientific examination of gender related to psychological functioning and behavior. Topics can include psychological research on human similarities and differences in gender attitudes, relationships, sexuality, violence, employment, and mental health.

PSY 527.subject: PSY
PSY 527.description: Introduces psychological theories and concepts pertaining to different racial groups in the United States. Explores historical and contemporary racism in the U.S. and its psychological effect on racial identity and the intersections of race, ethnicity, sex, gender identity, social class, and nationality. Explores racism and intersecting forms of oppression in the discipline of psychology. Develops cultural competence and humility to prepare students to live and work with individuals from diverse socio-cultural backgrounds.

PSY 531.subject: PSY
PSY 531.description: Neurobiological underpinnings of behavior examining animal and human research on neural structure and function in relation to typical and atypical behavior, including psychiatric disorders.

PSY 541.subject: PSY
PSY 541.description: Cognitive psychology studies the processes by which human beings notice, encode, remember, and use information. A graduate-level survey that covers the history, methods, important findings, and major theories of the field, with an emphasis on reading and critically analyzing articles from the primary research literature. Topics of interest will include perception and object recognition, attention, working memory, long-term memory, concepts and categorization, and judgment and decision making.

PSY 542.subject: PSY
PSY 542.description: Fundamental concepts of animal and human sensation and perception, with emphasis on audition and vision. Applications of psychophysical methods to research in all sensory modalities. Includes review workshops on basic mathematical, physical and physiological concepts necessary to interpret research in this field.

PSY 544.subject: PSY
PSY 544.description: Experimental and theoretical work on learning, conditioning, and memory in animals and humans.

PSY 546.subject: PSY
PSY 546.description: Explore biological, behavioral, perceptual, cognitive and social issues relevant to how humans interact with other computing technology from a psychological science perspective. Evaluate, design, and experimentally test human computer interactions using experimental methods in psychological science.

PSY 551.subject: PSY
PSY 551.description: Examines research theories, methods, and findings in lifespan developmental psychological science, with a focus on infancy, childhood, and late adulthood. Includes how social development in infancy and early childhood lay the foundation for social behavior in childhood, adolescence, and adulthood. Emphasizes cognitive topics and processes at multiple points of development. Considers how diversity in cognitive development can be best supported in communities.

PSY 552.subject: PSY
PSY 552.description: Explores meanings of culture. Examines topics in cognitive, social, developmental, and health psychology in light of various cultural backgrounds, orientations, and forces. Emphasizes contemporary applications of empirical findings from cross-cultural psychological research. Develops a historical, ecological, and global perception of psychology.

PSY 554.subject: PSY
PSY 554.description: Discusses intellectual development from infancy to adulthood. Topics include the origin of thinking, the development of perception, attention, memory, problem solving, language, academic skills, and social cognition. Piaget, Vygotsky, and information processing approaches will be discussed.

PSY 556.subject: PSY
PSY 556.description: Covers theories and research concerning human social development. Topics include theories of socialization; the development of social relationships; the self-concept; emotion; sex roles; social cognition; pro-social behavior; morality; self-control; and aggression.

PSY 557.subject: PSY
PSY 557.description: Examines autism and neurodiversity from a psychological perspective. Emphasizes the scientific basis of autism and neurodiversity, with an emphasis on research co-created with autistic researchers and reflecting the lived experience of autistic and neurodivergent individuals, including those with a range of support needs, in social context. Critically examines historical and current diagnostic criteria and processes, evidence-based therapies, interventions and supports, and inclusive workplace, educational, legal, and healthcare environments that allow autistic and neurodivergent people to enjoy fulfilling, interdependent lives in community with other neurotypical and neurodivergent people.

PSY 558.subject: PSY
PSY 558.description: Psychological processes involved in the acquisition and use of language throughout childhood. Biological, cognitive, and social influences on language will be discussed, as well as personal uses of language, such as language in thought and reading.

PSY 561.subject: PSY
PSY 561.description: A graduate level survey course of the theories, methods, and empirical findings that constitute the field of social psychology. Topics will include, but not be limited to, person perception, social cognition, attitudes, attitude change, persuasion, interpersonal attraction, relationships, small-group processes, altruism, and aggression.

PSY 562.subject: PSY
PSY 562.description: Examines disability from social psychological and disability studies perspectives. Emphasizes the social construction of disability and its inter- and intra-personal ramifications. Explores stereotyping, prejudice and discrimination, adaptation to disability, disability identity, working with people with disabilities, intersectionality, and sexuality.

PSY 571.subject: PSY
PSY 571.description: A graduate level introduction to psychological testing theory and practice, and to ethical, sociopolitical, psychological, and psychometric issues in the use of psychological tests. Particularly emphasizes basic psychometric principles that are important in scale construction, test evaluation, and practical assessment.
PSY 571.prerequisites_raw: ST 511 with B- or better and ST 512 [B-]

PSY 576.subject: PSY
PSY 576.description: Examines empirical findings, phenomena, and theories related to nonverbal behavior and its perception from a psychological perspective. Covers topics including: theories of nonverbal behavior encoding, decoding, and their accuracy; the neurophysiological basis for nonverbal behavior; valid assessments of nonverbal behavior abilities; and the impact that nonverbal behavior has on interaction processes and social relationships.

PSY 582.subject: PSY
PSY 582.description: Survey of the theory, techniques and research on the major contemporary systems of psychotherapy.

PSY 583.subject: PSY
PSY 583.description: Developmental perspective on child and adolescent psychological disorders including causal factors, associated features, and research-supported interventions.

PSY 584.subject: PSY
PSY 584.description: Focuses on the psychological factors in drug and behavioral addictions and associated interventions. The approach will be biopsychosocial, addressing neurobiological, behavioral, psychological, and social factors that influence addiction. Topics will include epidemiology and public health impact, diagnosis, models of addiction, and intervention and treatment approaches.

PSY 585.subject: PSY
PSY 585.description: Review of basics of operant and classical conditioning. Research on behavior modification and behavior therapy with both normal and abnormal animals, human adults, and children. Application areas include: behavior problems, handicaps, eating disorders, time management, self-control, stress management, contingency contracts, and cognitive therapies.
PSY 585.recommended: PSY 350 or equivalent work in family life or education.

PSY 588.subject: PSY
PSY 588.course_name: PSYCHOLOGY OF TRAUMA, OPPRESSION, AND RESILIENCE
PSY 588.description: Focuses on the psychological science of humans' reactions to traumatic events. Critically examines the social and cultural context for those events and reactions, including systemic racism, sexism, and other forms of oppression. Explores the psychological science of healing, resilience, and liberation, in the context of evidence-based clinical psychological treatments, institutional courage, and societal change.

PSY 594.subject: PSY
PSY 594.description: Survey human capabilities and limitations in human-machine interaction, including vision, memory, attention, motor control, and human error. Emphasis on theory and implications for system designs.

PSY 595.subject: PSY
PSY 595.description: Explores the psychological processes of meditation, and requires regular meditation sessions by students. Readings ranging from traditional Eastern philosophy to empirical psychological research journal articles will focus on outcomes and effective methods of meditation practice.

PSY 596.subject: PSY
PSY 596.description: Survey of psychological research and theory relevant to organizations, industry, and other work settings. Topics include training, employee selection, performance evaluation, work attitudes, and motivation.

PSY 598.subject: PSY
PSY 598.description: Psychological factors in the maintenance of good health and in the prevention of, treatment of, and recovery from illness: Behavioral contributions to illness, life-style risk factors, stress and the immune system, psychological response to symptoms and care-givers, health habits and self-care, management of pain and chronic illness, disability and terminal illness.

PSY 649.subject: PSY
PSY 649.description: Advanced survey of human information processing and performance in human-technology systems, with emphasis on theory, methodology, and implications for system analysis and design.

PSY 697.subject: PSY
PSY 697.course_name: GRADUATE PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCE OF TEACHING AND LEARNING
PSY 697.description: For graduate students of all majors on the translation of cognitive, social, and developmental psychological science for the practice of university teaching and learning. Topics include memory, attention, metacognition, motivation, interpersonal and developmental processes, and individual differences. Emphasis on critical review of theories and methods, and practical applications for university teaching.

PT 723.subject: PT
PT 723.description: Introduce and discuss issues and skills related to professionalism, psychosocial factors, and sociocultural factors that inform physical therapist practice. Explore professional behaviors, ethical decision making, and cultural competence/inclusion in depth.

PT 724.subject: PT
PT 724.description: Explores the theory and principles of patient care skills, emphasizing techniques often used to mobilize individuals in inpatient settings. Models and develops patient management, basic mobility skills (e.g., bed mobility, transfers, assisted locomotion) and long-term positioning programs for individuals with various impairments. Teaches body mechanics and ergonomic principles and incorporates consistent practice during labs. Techniques for stress reduction management are introduced. Presents equipment used in the acute care environment (“lines and tubes”) and infection control procedures. Emphasizes peer collaboration and skill practice.

PT 725.subject: PT
PT 725.description: Examines multiple aspects of the patient assessment conducted by a physical therapist that includes bony palpation, goniometric range of motion testing, and strength testing. Examines in-depth manual muscle testing with an additional emphasis on alternate methods of strength testing.

PT 726.subject: PT
PT 726.course_name: THERAPEUTIC EXERCISE I FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 726.description: Explores basic principles of therapeutic exercise and exercise progression for a general patient population. Examines patient safety and handling, proper and safe body mechanics for the therapist and patient, patient rapport building, education and communication. Explores patient-centered goal setting, use of the biopsychosocial model, integration of functional tasks and introduction to manual therapy.

PT 727.subject: PT
PT 727.course_name: THERAPEUTIC EXERCISE II FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 727.description: Applies principles of therapeutic exercise and related interventions to the upper and lower extremities. Integrates theory and skills specific to mobility, motor control, and muscle performance. Develops clinical decisions-making skills about interventions provided by physical therapists through interpretation of patient case scenarios. Provides learning opportunities for progressing and regressing interventions as appropriate.

PT 728.subject: PT
PT 728.course_name: THERAPEUTIC EXERCISE III FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 728.description: Applies prior knowledge and skills to increasingly complex patient cases and considers additional body systems in the application of therapeutic exercise and related interventions. Applies theory and skills of therapeutic exercise to the axial skeleton. Introduces the principles of aquatic therapy and develops interventions for balance, gait, and running deviations. Explores the use of therapeutic exercise for special populations and some musculoskeletal post-operative conditions.

PT 729.subject: PT
PT 729.description: Explores thermal, electrical and mechanical biophysical agents used by physical therapists in their comprehensive treatment intervention based on clinical research. Examines principles and application of common biophysical agents utilized by the physical therapist and will provide in-depth evidence-based criteria for selection, prescription, and implementation of these biophysical agents.

PT 732.subject: PT
PT 732.course_name: MUSCULOSKELETAL ANATOMY I FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 732.description: Examines musculoskeletal anatomy, innervation, blood supply, and function. Explores the upper and lower extremities using a regional approach.

PT 733.subject: PT
PT 733.course_name: MUSCULOSKELETAL ANATOMY II FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 733.description: Examines musculoskeletal anatomy, innervation, blood supply, and function. Explores the upper extremity, head, neck, and trunk using a regional approach.

PT 734.subject: PT
PT 734.description: Examines the structures in the brain, spinal cord and peripheral nervous systems. Demonstrates clinical assessments of these neurologic pathways and relate abnormal findings to functional impairment to introduce clinical thinking strategies when working with patients with neurologic dysfunction.

PT 735.subject: PT
PT 735.description: Builds on current anatomical knowledge to examine the musculoskeletal system from a biomechanical perspective. Includes a detailed kinesiologic analysis of the extremities and trunk, emphasizing joint structure and function, arthrokinematics, and muscle activation during joint movement. Discusses the effect of injury, strength deficits, and mobility impairments on quality of joint movement.

PT 736.subject: PT
PT 736.description: Builds on knowledge of joint structure and function from Clinical Biomechanics I to evaluate functional movement from a biomechanical perspective, with an emphasis on walking and running gait. Includes a detailed discussion of the principles of movement analysis and current technology in the field, as well as a critical appraisal of current biomechanical literature.

PT 737.subject: PT
PT 737.description: Explores terms used in disease, epidemiology, and pharmacology. Introduces fundamental concepts of disease, with specific focus on inflammatory, immune, and infectious contributors. Delineates normal versus pathological inflammatory and immune responses, with exploration of systemic effects caused by each. Applies core pharmacological principles such as pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics within the context of medical and physical therapy management of common pathological conditions. Presents pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment options for common pathologies, including medical and physical therapy management. Emphasizes safety considerations with respect to differential screening and recognition of medical complications that require precautions or represent contraindications to physical therapy treatment.

PT 738.subject: PT
PT 738.description: Analyzes neurophysiologic mechanisms underlying normal and abnormal motor and sensory function. Emphasis on pain processing, neuroplasticity and brain behavior relationships.

PT 739.subject: PT
PT 739.course_name: PATHOLOGY & PHARMACOLOGY FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 739.description: Emphasizes prevalent pathological diseases/conditions organized by body system. Explores the pathogenesis, incidence, prevalence, etiology, clinical manifestations, and treatment interventions (pharmacological, medical/surgical, physical therapy) for diseases/conditions. Explores wound management and cancer rehabilitation. Interactively explores direct interventions for lymphedema. Emphasizes systems screening and interpretation of medical conditions with precautions or contraindications for physical therapy interventions.

PT 742.subject: PT
PT 742.course_name: CLINICAL PHYSIOLOGY FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 742.description: Examines foundational bioenergetics, including the metabolic transformation of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins into energy and the use of metabolic by-products for gluconeogenesis. Explores the hormonal regulation of metabolism at rest and during exercise. Considers the definition, regulation, common uses, and effects of dietary supplements. Reviews other physiology systems including endocrine, renal, muscle, and integumentary. Examines common pathological conditions for select systems.

PT 744.subject: PT
PT 744.course_name: MOTOR CONTROL & LEARNING ACROSS THE LIFESPAN
PT 744.description: Examines motor control, motor learning, and recovery of function theories and their clinical application across the lifespan. Discusses normal and abnormal postural control, mobility, reach, grasp and object manipulation with an emphasis on synthesizing these theories into evidence-based clinical practice.

PT 747.subject: PT
PT 747.course_name: MOTOR DEVELOPMENT FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 747.description: Examines the processes and products of motor development covering the entire life span, including biological, affective, cognitive, and behavioral aspects.

PT 749.subject: PT
PT 749.description: Explores the physical and psycho-behavioral aspects of aging in adulthood with an emphasis on normal and pathological aging, clinical problems, and implications for therapeutic interventions delivered by the physical therapist. Examines modifiable disease risk factors impacting older adults’ lifespan in order to promote optimal care, functional outcomes, and wellness in older adults.

PT 751.subject: PT
PT 751.description: Explores the physical therapist’s examination, evaluation, diagnostic labeling, prognostication, intervention and outcome determination for the pediatric population (infants, children, and adolescents) using common pediatric medical diagnoses.

PT 753.subject: PT
PT 753.description: Explores normal physiology of the pulmonary and cardiovascular systems as well as pathogenesis and clinical presentation of common pathologies. Examines evaluation and interventions to optimize cardiovascular and pulmonary function in healthy individuals and those with impairments. Identifies common medical (surgical and pharmacological) and physical therapy interventions. Covers tests and measures, and direct interventions in laboratory sessions.

PT 754.subject: PT
PT 754.description: Explores examination, evaluation, diagnosis, prognosis, and interventions for orthopedic conditions of the upper extremities. Demonstrates integration of the information learned in year one as well as the experiential knowledge gained during clinical affiliations. Reviews lecture, guest lecturers, case studies, videos, volunteers and laboratory sessions for the practice and learning of orthopedic assessment and intervention techniques.

PT 755.subject: PT
PT 755.description: Explores examination, evaluation, diagnosis, prognosis, and interventions for orthopedic conditions of the lower extremities. Examines the integration of the information learned in year one as well as the experiential knowledge gained during clinical affiliations. Reviews lecture, guest lecturers, case studies, videos, volunteers and laboratory sessions for the practice and learning of orthopedic assessment and intervention techniques.

PT 756.subject: PT
PT 756.description: Explores the examination, evaluation, diagnosis, prognosis, and interventions for orthopedic conditions of the spine and the inter-relationships between axial and appendicular structures. Develops clinical competence in joint assessment and treatment techniques from a neuromusculoskeletal perspective, with emphasis on manual therapy techniques for the spine.

PT 757.subject: PT
PT 757.description: Examine excellence in sports physical therapy with an emphasis on promoting and advancing specific areas of sports physical therapy across the profession.

PT 758.subject: PT
PT 758.description: Prepares students to be able to demonstrate an examination and evaluation, develop a diagnosis and prognosis, and select and demonstrate interventions for adults with neurological dysfunction, with an emphasis on spinal cord injury. Reviews and applies principles of neuroanatomy, neuroscience, motor learning and motor control. Interprets examination and evaluation findings to create a patient-centered plan of care in collaboration with patient, family and interdisciplinary team members that considers the patient’s resources, environment, and capacity for recovery.

PT 759.subject: PT
PT 759.description: Prepares students to be able to demonstrate an examination and evaluation, develop a diagnosis and prognosis, and select and demonstrate interventions for adults with neurological dysfunction, with an emphasis on stroke, traumatic brain injury, concussion, brain tumor and demyelinating neurologic diseases. Reviews and applies principles of neuroanatomy, neuroscience, motor learning and motor control. Interprets examination and evaluation findings to create a patient-centered plan of care in collaboration with patient, family and interdisciplinary team members that considers the patient’s resources, environment, and capacity for recovery.

PT 762.subject: PT
PT 762.description: Prepares students to be able to demonstrate an examination and evaluation, develop a diagnosis and prognosis, and select and demonstrate interventions for adults with neurological dysfunction, with an emphasis on neurodegenerative diseases, vestibular pathologies, and balance and falls. Reviews and applies principles of neuroanatomy, neuroscience, motor learning and motor control. Interprets examination and evaluation findings to create a patient-centered plan of care in collaboration with patient, family and interdisciplinary team members that considers the patient’s resources, environment, and capacity for recovery.

PT 763.subject: PT
PT 763.description: Explores the multidimensional nature of pain, the biopsychosocial model as related to pain/ability/disability, assessment and measurement of pain, management of pain, clinical pain conditions, sociocultural influences on pain perception, concepts and tools to mitigate the psychological contribution to pain and disability, and the role and responsibility of the health care provider in mitigating pain without causing additional harm.

PT 764.subject: PT
PT 764.course_name: DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 764.description: Explores the skills necessary to perform a medical screening and differential diagnosis. Examines systems review, viscogenic and systemic origins of neuromusculoskeletal pain and dysfunction, integration of diagnostic imaging and laboratory testing in physical therapy diagnosis and referral management. Explores palpation and observation directed towards referral management strategies.

PT 766.subject: PT
PT 766.course_name: HEALTH PROMOTION & WELLNESS FOR THE PHYSICAL THERAPIST
PT 766.description: Explore the physical therapist’s role in promoting health and wellness at the individual and community levels, with emphasis on the rural health environment and underserved communities. Define population health, recognize how multiple determinants of health interact to influence health, identify key health indicators used to monitor population health, access sources of population health data to guide prevention and health promotion efforts, and learn to advocate for the health needs of society.

PT 767.subject: PT
PT 767.description: Discover and explore the unique needs of physical therapy and the health services environment in rural communities. Builds on content introduced in PT 766 . Provides students with an understanding of the unique aspects of the health services delivery system and other associated public and private systems that impact rehabilitation, health, and wellness in the rural United States. Emphasizes the diverse populations and needs of the Northwest and Mountain West regions of the United States.

PT 768.subject: PT
PT 768.description: Explores various aspects of physical therapy practice management. Examines the law, finance, operations, marketing, billing and coding and employment.

PT 769.subject: PT
PT 769.course_name: PROSTHETICS AND ORTHOTICS IN PHYSICAL THERAPY
PT 769.description: Examines prosthetics and orthotics and people with amputations. Examines surgical procedures for lower extremity (LE) and upper extremity (UE) amputations, components of LE and UE orthoses and prostheses as well as spinal orthoses. Explores physical therapy evaluation and treatment of individuals with amputations including interventions for gait abnormalities.

PT 770.subject: PT
PT 770.course_name: LEADERSHIP & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT IN PHYSICAL THERAPY
PT 770.description: Explores leadership and professional development as part of the art of being an effective physical therapist. Builds on students’ existing strengths to enhance and expand intrapersonal, interpersonal, professional and leadership skills. Introduces leadership theory and how leadership differs from management; development of a professional portfolio and personal development plan; leadership, teamwork, and followership in clinical and non-clinical settings; ethics and integrity in leadership; and the leader’s role in mentoring and developing future leaders.

PT 771.subject: PT
PT 771.description: Provides the physical therapy student with an overview of physical therapy specializations in a variety of areas.

PT 772.subject: PT
PT 772.description: Explores medical imaging for the physical therapist and covers principles and application of various medical imaging techniques, including X-ray and MRI.

PT 773.subject: PT
PT 773.course_name: EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE AND RESEARCH METHODS I
PT 773.description: Explores evidence-based practice, with a focus on the skills and knowledge needed during the first year in the DPT program. Emphasizes developing a clinical question, searching the literature for the best evidence, and critically appraising the evidence, with considerable time spent on navigating scholarly databases.

PT 774.subject: PT
PT 774.course_name: EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICE AND RESEARCH METHODS II
PT 774.description: Expands on concepts learned in PT 773 , with a focus on conducting clinical research, including study planning, design, and execution. Emphasizes research ethics, IRB, levels of evidence, statistical tests and measures, and the peer review/publication process.

PT 775.subject: PT
PT 775.description: Expands on concepts learned in PT 773 and PT 774 . Examines methods to prepare DPT graduates to communicate, implement and sustain evidence-based practices for the physical therapist at the individual and organizational level. Applies theories of implementation science, knowledge translation and dissemination science to prepare students to create an implementation plan of an evidenced-based physical therapy practice. Concludes with a culminating project to summarize and defend an action plan to ensure students are prepared to enter the profession with the tools needed to close the gap in implementation of evidence-based practices.

PT 776.subject: PT
PT 776.description: Builds on skills learned in the evidence-based practice sequence to prepare students to complete a group research project under the direction of a faculty mentor, including developing a thorough literature search, refining a clinical question and hypothesis, and identifying the necessary background knowledge and skills for their project.

PT 781.subject: PT
PT 781.description: Provides an opportunity for students to complete a group research project under the guidance of a faculty mentor over the span of three quarters. Applies skills learned in the research and evidence-based practice courses, with an emphasis on initiating data collection for the project.

PT 782.subject: PT
PT 782.description: Provides an opportunity for students to complete a group research project under the guidance of a faculty mentor over the span of three quarters. Continues the project initiated during PT 781 , with an emphasis on finishing data collection and initiating data analysis for the project.

PT 783.subject: PT
PT 783.description: Provides an opportunity for students to complete a group research project under the guidance of a faculty mentor over the span of three quarters. Completes the project initiated during PT 781 and continued during PT 782 , with an emphasis on finishing data analysis, writing a scientific manuscript, and giving a final research presentation.

PT 784.subject: PT
PT 784.description: Focuses on core principles of community engagement for physical therapy practice, research, and leadership. Explores a model of care in which physical therapists work with their community in a partnership role, a model of care that has the potential to foster relationships in which innovative solutions to community problems, including societal health, can be created. Emphasizes the principles of community engagement and community building, expanding physical therapy students’ knowledge in how to engage their community.

PT 785.subject: PT
PT 785.description: Provides the opportunity to actively participate in a community-engaged project with a local community partner organization for the mutually beneficial exchange of knowledge and resources. Implements a project that may enrich health through skilled physical therapy, prepare educated and engaged citizens, strengthen democratic values and civic responsibility, address critical societal issues, and contribute to the public good. Applies the principles of community engagement and community building through participation in a project.

PT 789.subject: PT
PT 789.description: Emphasizes and expands the integration of the patient client management process, clinical reasoning, professional behavior, and psychomotor skills involving patients or clients with complex health conditions, systems thinking, case management challenges, and interrelated ethical and biopsychosocial factors. Provides training to identify next steps in plans of care, with emphasis on interventions, physical therapy discharge, coordination and transfer of care, and transition to wellness/health promotion activities.

PT 792.subject: PT
PT 792.description: Practice professional behaviors, communication skills, and examination and intervention techniques in a clinical setting. Work in pairs with clinical instructor(s) at an assigned clinical facility to practice skills and behaviors learned in past classes and integrate new skills learned concurrently in other courses. Identify and practice new examination and intervention techniques. Provide clinical instruction at a local or out of town facility by qualified, experienced physical therapists.

PT 793.subject: PT
PT 793.description: Practice professional behaviors, communication skills, and examination and intervention techniques in a clinical setting. Work in pairs with clinical instructor(s) at an assigned clinical facility to practice skills and behaviors learned in past classes and integrate new skills learned concurrently in other courses. Identify and practice new examination and intervention techniques. Provides clinical instruction at a local or out of town facility by qualified, experienced physical therapists.

PT 794.subject: PT
PT 794.description: Provides students with their first opportunity to practice professional behaviors, communication skills, and examination and intervention techniques in a full-time clinical schedule. Work in pairs with clinical instructor(s) at an assigned clinical facility to practice and integrate skills and behaviors learned in past classes. Identify and practice new examination and intervention techniques. Provides clinical instruction a local or out of town facility by qualified, experienced physical therapists.

PT 795.subject: PT
PT 795.description: Provides students with their second opportunity to practice professional behaviors, communication skills, examination, evaluation, planning and intervention techniques in a full-time clinical experience. Work with clinical instructor(s) at an assigned clinical facility to practice skills and behaviors learned in past classes and integrate new skills learned concurrently in other courses. Identify and practice new examination and intervention techniques. Provides clinical instruction at a local or out of town facility by qualified, experienced physical therapists.

PT 796.subject: PT
PT 796.description: Provides students with their first ten-week terminal clinical experience following completion of their didactic coursework. Works with Clinical Instructor(s) at an assigned clinical facility to practice and apply skills and behaviors learned in past classes and demonstrate increasing levels of independence in practice. Identifies and practices new examination and intervention techniques, at the Clinical Instructor’s discretion. Provides clinical instruction at a local or out of town facility by qualified, experienced physical therapists.

PT 797.subject: PT
PT 797.description: Provides students with their second ten-week terminal clinical experience following completion of their didactic coursework. Works with Clinical Instructor(s) at an assigned clinical facility to practice and apply skills and behaviors learned in past classes and demonstrate increasing levels of independence in practice. Identifies and practices new examination and intervention techniques, at the Clinical Instructor’s discretion. Provides clinical instruction at a local or out of town facility by qualified, experienced physical therapists.

PT 798.subject: PT
PT 798.description: Provides students with their third and final ten-week terminal clinical experience following completion of their didactic coursework. Works with Clinical Instructor(s) at an assigned clinical facility to practice and apply skills and behaviors learned in past classes and demonstrate increasing levels of independence in practice. Identifies and practices new examination and intervention techniques, at the Clinical Instructor’s discretion. Provides clinical instruction at a local or out of town facility by qualified, experienced physical therapists.

QS 262.subject: QS
QS 262.description: Centering itself on activism and scholarship, this course examines homophobia's and transphobia's relationship with racism, colonialism, sexism, ableism, classism and other forms of oppression. Introduces key concepts, histories, and political frameworks within Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer political movements. CROSSLISTED as QS 262 / WGSS 262 . (Bacc Core Course)

QS 262H.subject: QS
QS 262H.description: Centering itself on activism and scholarship, this course examines homophobia's and transphobia's relationship with racism, colonialism, sexism, ableism, classism and other forms of oppression. Introduces key concepts, histories, and political frameworks within Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer political movements. CROSSLISTED as QS 262 / WGSS 262 . (Bacc Core Course).

QS 275.subject: QS
QS 275.description: Explores concepts of structural inequality, difference, power, and discrimination through a critical survey of arts activism. Requires critical thinking about artwork and artists which address a number of social issues in the United States, including race, ethnicity, class, gender, sexuality, immigration, and Indigeneity. Emphasizes various practicing artists and academics with a focus on counter narratives, intersectionality, fluid and multiple identities and communities while also examining many genres of art activism and readings. Includes a strong focus on Indigeneity. CROSSLISTED as ES 275 / QS 275 / WGSS 275 .
attributes: CFAH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities General; CPDP – Bacc Core

QS 321.subject: QS
QS 321.description: Examines the concept of Queer popular culture through film, music, TV, image, and other mediums. Seeks to disrupt dominant discourses around gender and sexuality by centralizing women of color feminisms and queer of color critiques to analyze popular representations of gender, sexuality, race, class, disability, and other social locations. CROSSLISTED as QS 321 / WGSS 321 . (Bacc Core Course)

QS 362.subject: QS
QS 362.description: Engages the ethics and responsibilities involved in serving LGBTQ+ communities in fields such as education, health, law, and social services for those entering and/or continuing professions in fields that historically underserve LGBTQ+ people. Topics include LGBTQ+ youth; LGBTQ+ elders; issues affecting LGBTQ+ people across their lifespans; approaches to cultural competency; violence against LGBTQ+ people, forms of oppression including heterosexism, homophobia, and transphobia; and LGBTQ+ community resilience. CROSSLISTED as QS 362 / WGSS 362 . (Bacc Core Course)

QS 364.subject: QS
QS 364.description: Addresses transgender politics--including non-binary and gender non-conforming issues--through feminist and intersectional approaches by analyzing transgender theories, arts, and activism. CROSSLISTED as QS 364 / WGSS 364 .

QS 364H.subject: QS
QS 364H.description: Addresses transgender politics--including non-binary and gender non-conforming issues--through feminist and intersectional approaches by analyzing transgender theories, arts, and activism. CROSSLISTED as QS 364 / WGSS 364 .

QS 409.subject: QS
QS 409.description: Capstone projects bring theory into practice through research, design, and implementation of a project that synthesizes and demonstrates learning in the Queer Studies program.

QS 431.subject: QS
QS 431.description: "Queer of color critiques" refers to political theories and activism that emerge from LGBTQ people of color to examine the intersections between race, sexuality and gender. Addresses these intersections through theory, history, and activism. CROSSLISTED as ES 431 / QS 431 / WGSS 431 and ES 531 / QS 531 / WGSS 531 .

QS 432.subject: QS
QS 432.description: A creative and discussion-based course focusing on ways in which photography can and has addressed issues of gender and sexuality. An introduction to key concepts and intersections in Women's, Gender and Sexuality Studies; Queer Studies and photography theory. Create written and photographic responses to artworks, texts, personal experience and pop-culture. CROSSLISTED as ART 432 / QS 432 / WGSS 432 and ART 532 / QS 532 .

QS 449.subject: QS
QS 449.description: Explores Indigenous feminisms as well as some of the issues facing Indigenous women in the Americas and Pacific Islands. Relates Indigenous feminisms to the complexity of federal law and policies as well as land struggles between Indigenous communities and contemporary settler colonial nations. Raises awareness of current Indigenous struggles as well as Indigenous feminist responses and resistance to these same struggles. CROSSLISTED as ES 449 / QS 449 / WGSS 449 .
QS 449.recommended: Critical thinking, evaluation, and synthesis skills

QS 462.subject: QS
QS 462.description: Engages key themes and critical frameworks in queer theories. Topics include histories of sexuality; forms of oppression, including heterosexism, homophobia, and transphobia; resistance to oppression; violence against LGBTQ people; queer activism; diverse experiences of sexuality; and representations in literature, art, and popular media. CROSSLISTED as QS 462 / WGSS 462 and QS 562 / WGSS 562 .

QS 472.subject: QS
QS 472.description: "Two-spirit" refers to North American indigenous genders outside of European male/female binaries. Two-spirit communities argue for decolonization as a central political struggle, calling all people to unlearn settler colonial gender/sexuality on Native land. Addresses indigenous two-spirit/GLBTQ issues through theory, literature, activism, and art. CROSSLISTED as QS 472 / WGSS 472 .
attributes: CSWC – Core Ed - Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); CWIC – Bacc Core

QS 473.subject: QS
QS 473.description: With a particular focus on transgender people of color and transnational constructions of gender, engages issues in the lives of Transgender people through autobiography, memoir, biography, poetry, and documentary film. CROSSLISTED as QS 473 / WGSS 473 and QS 573 / WGSS 573 .

QS 476.subject: QS
QS 476.description: Explores contemporary experiences of sexualities within transnational contexts. Analyzes themes including queer and LGBTQI organizing, same-sex desires, queer transnational immigration and labor flows, sex industries and discourses of trafficking, sex tourism, and reproductive justice, using feminist, queer, and postcolonial theoretical frameworks. CROSSLISTED as QS 476 / WGSS 476 and QS 576 / WGSS 576 .
QS 476.prerequisites_raw: QS 262 with D- or better or QS 262H with D- or better or WGSS 262 with D- or better or WGSS 262H with D- or better

QS 477.subject: QS
QS 477.course_name: QUEER/TRANS PEOPLE OF COLOR ARTS AND ACTIVISM
QS 477.description: LGBTQ people of color often engage struggles for social justice through artistic movements. Focuses on arts by LGBTQ people of color and the way these artistic movements contribute to activism that interrupts interlocking systems of oppression. CROSSLISTED as ES 477 / QS 477 / WGSS 477 and ES 577/ QS 577 / WGSS 577 .

QS 499.subject: QS
QS 499.description: Topics in gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, and queer issues and scholarship. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.

QS 524.subject: QS
QS 524.description: Addresses transgender politics--including transsexual, genderqueer, and gender non-conforming issues--through feminist and intersectional approaches by analyzing transgender theories, arts, and activism. CROSSLISTED as QS 524 / WGSS 524 .

QS 531.subject: QS
QS 531.description: "Queer of color critiques" refers to political theories and activism that emerge from LGBTQ people of color to examine the intersections between race, sexuality and gender. Addresses these intersections through theory, history, and activism. CROSSLISTED as ES 431 / QS 431 / WGSS 431 and ES 531 / QS 531 / WGSS 531 .

QS 532.subject: QS
QS 532.course_name: GENDER, SEXUALITY, AND THE PHOTOGRAPHIC IMAGE
QS 532.description: A creative and discussion-based course focusing on ways in which photography can and has addressed issues of gender and sexuality. An introduction to key concepts and intersections in Women's, Gender and Sexuality Studies; Queer Studies and photography theory. Create written and photographic responses to artworks, texts, personal experience and pop-culture. CROSSLISTED as ART 432 / QS 432 / WGSS 432 and ART 532 / QS 532 .

Relates Indigenous feminisms to the complexity of federal law and policies as well as land struggles between Indigenous communities and contemporary settler colonial nations. Raises awareness of current Indigenous struggles as well as Indigenous feminist responses and resistance to these same struggles. CROSSLISTED as ES 549 / QS 549 / WGSS 549 .

Two-spirit communities argue for decolonization as a central political struggle, calling all people to unlearn settler colonial gender/sexuality on Native land. Addresses indigenous two-spirit/GLBTQ issues through theory, literature, activism, and art. CROSSLISTED as QS 472 / WGSS 472 and QS 572 / WGSS 572 .

QS 573.subject: QS
QS 573.description: With a particular focus on transgender people of color and transnational constructions of gender, engages issues in the lives of Transgender people through autobiography, memoir, biography, poetry, and documentary film. CROSSLISTED as QS 473 / WGSS 473 and QS 573 / WGSS 573 .

QS 576.description: Explores contemporary experiences of sexualities within transnational contexts. Analyzes themes including queer and LGBTQI organizing, same-sex desires, queer transnational immigration and labor flows, sex industries and discourses of trafficking, sex tourism, and reproductive justice, using feminist, queer, and postcolonial theoretical frameworks. CROSSLISTED as QS 476 / WGSS 476 and QS 576 / WGSS 576 .
