Evaluates strategies to manage specific issues and applies course material to specific case studies.

TRAL 593.subject: TRAL
TRAL 593.description: Interpretation of natural and cultural features in parks, museums, and similar settings. Emphasis on learning and applying effective communication techniques in the development of brochures, exhibits, talks, museums, and visitor centers.

UEXP 002.subject: UEXP
UEXP 002.description: Provides students with basic personal and interpersonal leadership skills that can be used within and outside of a work setting. Through practice, the leadership experience helps students explore motivation, decision-making, time management, power, team building, conflict, ethics, dealing with change, communication skills, and diversity issues.

UEXP 003.subject: UEXP
UEXP 003.description: Engage in research activities appropriate to the discipline and through the research experience, acquire skills, techniques, and knowledge relevant to the field of study.

UEXP 406.subject: UEXP
UEXP 406.description: Trains new ambassadors to lead campus and housing tours. Creates educated, ethically and morally responsible, fully confident TOUR (Team of Undergraduate Recruiters) Ambassadors who are engaged, reflective, creative, and caring members of their communities who can contribute to the success of prospective and new students.

VMB 110.subject: VMB
VMB 110.description: Introduction to the profession's role in society.

VMB 112.subject: VMB
VMB 112.course_name: THE ONE HEALTH PARADIGM AND AUDIENCE CONNECTIONS
VMB 112.description: Present, discuss and communicate current research papers and ongoing projects in concise, audience appropriate formats using techniques from entrepreneurism, grant proposal writing and Hollywood storytelling.

VMB 415.subject: VMB
VMB 415.description: One health is the concept that human, animal and environmental health are all intertwined. Utilizes current one health issues such as disease outbreaks and antimicrobial resistance to encourage students from diverse fields to develop interdisciplinary collaboration and communication skills. CROSSLISTED as BHS 415 / VMB 415 .

VMB 424.subject: VMB
VMB 424.description: Offer comprehensive insights and essential tools to understand the core concepts and real-world applications of precision medicine, both its opportunities and challenges. Bridge the gap from laboratory research to clinical application and population health impact and equip students with a foundational knowledge to navigate through this evolving field. Encourage a holistic understanding of precision medicine's multidimensional landscape.
VMB 424.prerequisites_raw: ( BI 311 with D- or better or BI 311H with D- or better or BB 314 with D- or better or BB 314H with D- or better) and ( BHS 316 [D-] or MB 416 [D-])

VMB 499.subject: VMB
VMB 499.description: Special studies course to allow different instructors the ability to teach a new class or one time class.

VMB 512.subject: VMB
VMB 512.course_name: THE ONE HEALTH PARADIGM AND AUDIENCE CONNECTIONS
VMB 512.description: Present, discuss and communicate current research papers and ongoing projects in concise, audience appropriate formats using techniques from entrepreneurism, grant proposal writing and Hollywood storytelling.

VMB 517.subject: VMB
VMB 517.description: Physiology of body fluids, muscles, membranes, intermediary metabolism, cardiovascular system, and metabolism.

VMB 518.subject: VMB
VMB 518.description: Physiology of gastrointestinal, endocrine and reproductive systems.

VMB 519.subject: VMB
VMB 519.description: Physiology of respiratory and renal systems and acid-base balance.

VMB 523.subject: VMB
VMB 523.description: Interactive examination of the molecular basis of diseases that are transmissible between animals and humans. Emphasis on bacterial, viral and parasitic pathogens of animals and humans.

VMB 524.subject: VMB
VMB 524.description: Offer comprehensive insights and essential tools to understand the core concepts and real-world applications of precision medicine, both its opportunities and challenges. Bridge the gap from laboratory research to clinical application and population health impact and equip students with a foundational knowledge to navigate through this evolving field. Encourage a holistic understanding of precision medicine's multidimensional landscape.
VMB 524.recommended: Prior courses in immunology, microbiology, biochemistry, and physiology

VMB 611.subject: VMB
VMB 611.description: Systematic and topographic study and dissection of the dog, cat, horse, ruminant, pig, and chicken.

VMB 612.subject: VMB
VMB 612.description: Systematic and topographic study and dissection of the dog, cat, horse, ruminant, pig, and chicken.

VMB 614.subject: VMB
VMB 614.description: Structure and development of cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems of animals.

VMB 616.subject: VMB
VMB 616.description: Structural and functional relationships of the nervous system and organs of special sense with emphasis on general clinical application.

VMB 620.subject: VMB
VMB 620.description: Clinical and diagnostic aspects of immunological mechanisms, serological reactions; hypersensitivity, allergy, and disorders of the immune system.

VMB 621.subject: VMB
VMB 621.description: General principles of pathology, cell injury and death, inflammation and tissue repair, abnormalities of cell growth, and structures and mechanisms of disease.

VMB 622.subject: VMB
VMB 622.prerequisites_raw: VMB 611 (may be taken concurrently) with C or better

VMB 624.subject: VMB
VMB 624.description: Elective course for students to learn about significant aspects of antibiotic resistance. Intended to become part of the “One Health Program”, resulting in the ability to create a plan for effective antibiotic stewardship as it relates to human, animal, and environmental health.

VMB 627.subject: VMB
VMB 627.description: An introduction to the basic principles of ornamental fish medicine including basic husbandry, handling and clinical procedures. This is a 1-week intensive course held at the Hatfield Marine Science Center in Newport, Oregon. Graded P/N.

VMB 630.subject: VMB
VMB 630.description: Cellular and molecular events that contribute to the pathogenesis of disease in animals, including humans. Host interactions with infectious agents and the environment.

VMB 631.subject: VMB
VMB 631.description: The use of mathematical modeling in biological sciences is studied. A variety of modeling techniques are covered including implementing the methods computationally.

VMB 640.subject: VMB
VMB 640.description: Prepares students for careers in laboratory animal medicine. Provides a review of medical conditions, diagnosis and treatment of research animals.

VMB 641.subject: VMB
VMB 641.description: Prepares students for careers in laboratory animal medicine. Provides a review of medical conditions, diagnosis and treatment for research animals.

VMB 642.subject: VMB
VMB 642.description: Prepares students for careers in laboratory animal medicine. Provides a review of medical conditions, diagnosis and treatment for research animals.

VMB 651.subject: VMB
VMB 651.description: Topics vary; check Schedule of Classes for particular topics.

VMB 652.subject: VMB
VMB 652.description: Overview of systems biology approaches that are being used to study cancer, with an emphasis on omics techniques and fundamental mechanisms in the origination and progression of cancer. Discussion-based, with each class session focused on a contemporary research article in the field of cancer systems biology.

VMB 653.subject: VMB
VMB 653.description: Virology for the professional and graduate student.

VMB 659.subject: VMB
VMB 659.description: Veterinary bacteriology and mycology for the veterinary graduate student.

VMB 660.subject: VMB
VMB 660.description: A study of the parasitic diseases of domestic animals with an emphasis on diagnosis and treatment. Fundamentals in host-parasite interactions, taxonomy and life cycle strategies are covered.

VMB 663.subject: VMB
VMB 663.description: Practical hands-on course training students in the diagnostic pathology utilizing case material received at the OSU Veterinary Diagnostic Lab.

VMB 664.subject: VMB
VMB 664.description: Trains participants in the recognition, description, and pathogenesis of a wide variety of disease processes with an emphasis on microscopic features.

VMB 665.subject: VMB
VMB 665.description: Group discussions of assigned readings central to understanding of veterinary pathology, including recent advances.

VMB 666.subject: VMB
VMB 666.description: Covers aspects of veterinary medicine that affect human health. An understanding of the contribution of the veterinary profession to human (public) health will enable students to play an effective role in this area, regardless of career direction.

VMB 669.subject: VMB
VMB 669.description: To introduce students to the fundamentals of writing grant proposals to the National Institute of Health (NIH), different funding mechanisms, as well as the grant reviewing process. CROSSLISTED as PHAR 669 / VMB 669 .

VMB 670.subject: VMB
VMB 670.course_name: INTRODUCTION TO SYSTEMS BIOMEDICINE AND PHARMACOGENOMICS
VMB 670.description: Evaluates and explains ‘next generation’ approaches used in systems biomedicine and pharmacogenomics fields, including but not limited to large scale ‘omics’ data analysis and their integration in biological networks for novel understanding of disease mechanisms, improvement of diagnosis, prognosis and therapies. CROSSLISTED as PHAR 670 / VMB 670 .

VMB 671.subject: VMB
VMB 671.description: Intended for personnel with some scientific background who are seeking basic- and advanced-level molecular biology knowledge and who wish to become involved with molecular biology-related and biotechnological research.

VMB 673.subject: VMB
VMB 673.description: Examines immune system function in animals other than mice and men with a focus on adapting cutting-edge technologies.

VMB 674.subject: VMB
VMB 674.description: Provides students with a cohesive understanding of the basic research behind the discovery of new therapeutic targets and scientific advancements used in development of vaccines and new therapies.

VMB 675.subject: VMB
VMB 675.description: Explores personalized nutrition options for prevention and management of various diseases, including kidney, diabetes, liver, bone, oncology and more. Examines recent literature findings relevant to these organ systems. Provides opportunities for choosing topics of a particular interest for a deeper dive. CROSSLISTED as NUTR 675 / VMB 675 .

VMB 711.subject: VMB
VMB 711.description: Systematic and topographic study and dissection of the dog, cat, horse, ruminant, pig, and chicken.

VMB 712.subject: VMB
VMB 712.description: Systematic and topographic study and dissection of the dog, cat, horse, ruminant, pig, and chicken.

VMB 713.subject: VMB
VMB 713.description: Systematic and topographic study and dissection of the dog, cat, horse, ruminant, pig, and chicken. Lec/lab.

VMB 714.subject: VMB
VMB 714.description: Structure and development of cells, tissues, organs, and organ systems of animals.

VMB 716.subject: VMB
VMB 716.description: Structural and functional relationships of the nervous system and organs of special sense with emphasis on general clinical application.

VMB 717.subject: VMB
VMB 717.description: Physiology of body fluids, excretion, respiration, acid-base balance, blood, muscle, bone, cardiovascular system, digestion, metabolism, endocrine system, reproduction, and lactation.

VMB 718.subject: VMB
VMB 718.description: Physiology of body fluids, excretion, respiration, acid-base balance, blood, muscle, bone, cardiovascular system, digestion, metabolism, endocrine system, reproduction, and lactation.

VMB 719.subject: VMB
VMB 719.description: Physiology of body fluids, excretion, respiration, acid-base balance, blood, muscle, bone, cardiovascular system, digestion, metabolism, endocrine system, reproduction, and lactation.

VMB 720.subject: VMB
VMB 720.description: Clinical and diagnostic aspects of immunological mechanisms, serological reactions, hypersensitivity, allergy, and disorders of the immune system.

VMB 721.subject: VMB
VMB 721.description: Basic mechanisms and concepts relating to reaction of cells and tissues to disease, with emphasis on cellular and tissue degeneration, inflammatory reaction, circulatory disturbance and neoplasia.

VMB 722.subject: VMB
VMB 722.course_name: RESEARCH READING SKILLS FOR VETERINARY STUDENTS
VMB 722.description: Training in critical evaluation of biomedical and clinical research studies, and understanding of laboratory diagnostic methods.

VMB 724.subject: VMB
VMB 724.description: Elective course for students to learn about significant aspects of antibiotic resistance. Intended to become part of the “One Health Program”, resulting in the ability to create a plan for effective antibiotic stewardship as it relates to human, animal, and environmental health.

VMB 725.subject: VMB
VMB 725.description: Emphasizes clinically important anatomical structures through a body systems approach. Interactively solidifies critical microanatomy concepts and applies problem-solving skills. Emphasizes anatomical knowledge in relation to practical clinical cases in both small and large animals.
VMB 725.prerequisites_raw: VMB 711 with C- or better and VMB 712 [C-] and VMB 714 [C-]

VMB 727.subject: VMB
VMB 727.description: An introduction to the basic principles of ornamental fish medicine including basic husbandry, handling and clinical procedures.

VMB 728.subject: VMB
VMB 728.description: Focuses on diagnosis, treatment, and management of special animals, including the common laboratory animals.

VMB 729.subject: VMB
VMB 729.description: Designed to provide hands-on experience with a variety of laboratory animal species including primates, rodents, ungulates, fish, and reptiles. May be repeated up to 4 times for 3, 6, 9 or 12 credits per term. 12 credits maximum apply toward graduation. Graded P/N.

VMB 736.subject: VMB
VMB 736.description: One week clinical experience in clinical pathology, cytology, urinalysis, clinical chemistry interpretation and hematology.

VMB 749.subject: VMB
VMB 749.description: Clinical training in the care of exotic and zoo animal species. Graded P/N.

VMB 750.subject: VMB
VMB 750.description: Examines the principles of system and organ responses to injury and the consequent effects of these changes on the host.

VMB 751.subject: VMB
VMB 751.description: Examines the principles of system and organ responses to injury and the consequent effects of these changes on the host.

VMB 753.subject: VMB
VMB 753.description: Virology for the professional DVM student.

VMB 756.subject: VMB
VMB 756.description: One-week rotation in advanced clinical pathology: cytology, hematology and clinical chemistry interpretation.

VMB 759.subject: VMB
VMB 759.description: Bacteriology and mycology for the professional DVM student.

VMB 760.subject: VMB
VMB 760.description: A study of the parasitic diseases of domestic animals with an emphasis on diagnosis and treatment. Fundamentals in host-parasite interactions, taxonomy and life cycle strategies are covered.

VMB 761.subject: VMB
VMB 761.description: Fundamentals of pharmacology as related to veterinary medicine presented in a systems-oriented approach with drug therapy in domestic animals.

VMB 762.subject: VMB
VMB 762.description: Fundamentals of pharmacology as related to veterinary medicine presented in a systems-oriented approach with drug therapy in domestic animals.

VMB 763.subject: VMB
VMB 763.description: Clinical pathology for the professional DVM student.

VMB 765.subject: VMB
VMB 765.description: A study of toxic agents, mechanisms of action, toxicosis and treatments, especially as related to domestic and wild animals, with principles of toxicity testing, clinical diagnosis, and identification of poisonous plants. Lec/lab.

VMB 766.subject: VMB
VMB 766.description: Examination of the application of epidemiology to the field of veterinary medicine and the study of important veterinary public health issues.

VMB 768.subject: VMB
VMB 768.description: A rotation in histopathology at the Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory. Emphasis is placed on case evaluation, diagnosis and report writing of biopsies of all species. Graded P/N.

VMB 772.subject: VMB
VMB 772.description: Veterinary students work with veterinarians and domestic animals in international settings.

VMB 786.subject: VMB
VMB 786.description: A rotation in histopathology at the Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory. Emphasis is placed on case evaluation, diagnosis and report writing of biopsies of all species.

VMB 795.subject: VMB
VMB 795.description: Students will perform service duty in the necropsy area of the Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory and will perform necropsies on delivered specimens.

VMC 509.subject: VMC
VMC 509.course_name: TEACHING PRACTICUM FOR VETERINARY PROFESSIONAL CURRICULUM
VMC 509.description: Provides veterinary specialty residents and graduate students a mentored experience in teaching of veterinary medical students. Experience can be gained with teaching of lecture and/or laboratory courses.

VMC 632.subject: VMC
VMC 632.description: An interactive, practical course on the role of scholarship in clinical medicine, including techniques to develop and conduct research in a clinical setting.

VMC 634.subject: VMC
VMC 634.description: An interactive, practical course on the role of scholarship in clinical surgery, including techniques to develop and conduct research in a clinical setting.

VMC 682.subject: VMC
VMC 682.description: In-depth investigation of important topics in physiology, pathophysiology, treatment, diagnosis, and other aspects of internal medicine through investigation of primary literature and recent reviews.

VMC 684.subject: VMC
VMC 684.description: In-depth investigation of important topics in physiology, pathophysiology, treatment, diagnosis, and other aspects of surgery through investigation of primary literature and recent reviews.

VMC 711.subject: VMC
VMC 711.description: A one-week clinical elective rotation in cardiology at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital. May be repeated up to 4 times, two weeks or more is encouraged. Fourth-year standing in Veterinary Medicine required.

VMC 712.subject: VMC
VMC 712.description: A one-week clinical elective rotation in clinical oncology at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital. May be repeated up to 4 times, two weeks or more is encouraged. Fourth-year standing in Veterinary Medicine required.

VMC 713.subject: VMC
VMC 713.description: Introduces the clinical art and practice of small animal veterinary dentistry. Builds upon the review of anatomy and pathology introduced in the prior veterinary curriculum to create understanding of the tenants of general practice companion animal veterinary dentistry: periodontics, endodontics, oral medicine, and oral surgery.

VMC 714.subject: VMC
VMC 714.description: A clinical course designed to provide students with hands-on training in diagnosis, treatment and prophylaxis of dental diseases of dogs and cats.

VMC 715.subject: VMC
VMC 715.course_name: CASE STUDIES IN SMALL ANIMAL MEDICINE I
VMC 715.description: A case-based course involving diseases and conditions of the endocrine, gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary systems as well as neoplastic and infectious diseases of small animals.

VMC 716.subject: VMC
VMC 716.course_name: CASE STUDIES IN SMALL ANIMAL MEDICINE II
VMC 716.description: A case-based course involving diseases and conditions of the cardiovascular, respiratory and urogenital systems as well as emergent diseases and conditions.

VMC 717.subject: VMC
VMC 717.course_name: CASE STUDIES IN SMALL ANIMAL MEDICINE III
VMC 717.description: A case-based course involving diseases and conditions of the dermatologic, neurologic, ophthalmalogic, and hemolymphatic systems.

VMC 718.subject: VMC
VMC 718.description: Introductory course to basic concepts in small animal preventive medicine including vaccine immunology, vaccine strategies, internal/external parasite control, nutrition in disease prevention, and wellness programs for dogs and cats.

VMC 719.subject: VMC
VMC 719.description: Hands-on practical experience in a clinical setting in taking a clinical history, performing a cardiovascular physical examinations, recording electrocardiograms, interpreting thoracic radiographs and echocardiograms, creating problem lists, compiling lists of differential diagnosis, formulating diagnostic and therapeutic plans, discussing treatment options, generating medical records, and discharging patients.

VMC 720.subject: VMC
VMC 720.description: To examine the nutritional needs of many species of veterinary importance. Emphasis is placed on designing feeding programs to optimize health and animal performance.

VMC 721.subject: VMC
VMC 721.description: Introduction to the concepts of small animal clinical nutrition and is designed for the third-year veterinary student.

VMC 722.subject: VMC
VMC 722.description: Develop the knowledge, skills, and attitudes necessary to recognize patients requiring urgent or emergent care, initiate appropriate care, and become active members of the care team in the ER and ICU setting. The rotation is a mixture of supervised clinical experiences, hands-on patient care experience, deliberate practice of procedural skills, topic rounds, and case discussions.

VMC 723.subject: VMC
VMC 723.description: A one-week elective for senior students in the DVM curriculum. The course emphasizes aspects of internal medicine specific to the domestic cat. Graded P/N.

VMC 724.subject: VMC
VMC 724.description: Familiarizes students with general surgical principles and common surgical conditions in large animal species.

VMC 725.subject: VMC
VMC 725.description: A basic course in the principles and techniques of surgery for the professional veterinary student. Lec/lab.

VMC 726.subject: VMC
VMC 726.description: Advanced clinical experience in small animal (canine) reproduction. Graded P/N.

VMC 727.subject: VMC
VMC 727.description: Improve surgical skills and acquire more advanced knowledge of specific surgical conditions.

VMC 728.subject: VMC
VMC 728.description: Introduces general overview of veterinary pharmacy practice which includes, but is not limited to, regulatory aspects, prescription writing, controlled substances, unique challenges, drug compounding, general pharmacokinetics on commonly used Veterinary Teaching Hospital medications, pharmacy calculations, and practical applications.

VMC 729.subject: VMC
VMC 729.description: Practical and theoretical training in reproductive management and disorders in all species; routine diagnostic and treatment procedures; clinic rounds.

VMC 730.subject: VMC
VMC 730.course_name: LARGE ANIMAL MEDICINE AND SURGERY LABORATORY
VMC 730.description: Covers practical laboratory that allows students to develop skills necessary for physical examination and common diagnostic and surgical procedures on domestic large animal species, primarily horses and ruminants.

VMC 731.subject: VMC
VMC 731.description: A two-week clinical rotation at the Dove Lewis Memorial Emergency Clinic in Portland, OR.

VMC 732.subject: VMC
VMC 732.description: Clinical medicine training in diseases of food animals and horses; clinic rounds and diagnostic procedures.

VMC 733.subject: VMC
VMC 733.description: Apply surgery principles and common surgical procedures of large animal species

VMC 734.subject: VMC
VMC 734.description: Clinical surgery, treatment, and care of food animals and horses; clinical rounds; training in surgery, lameness, and diagnostic procedures.

VMC 735.subject: VMC
VMC 735.description: Rural practice training in diseases of food animals and horses.

VMC 736.subject: VMC
VMC 736.course_name: CLINICAL SKILLS IV: PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION AND ETHICS
VMC 736.description: Develop communication skills and ethical reasoning for client interactions.

VMC 737.subject: VMC
VMC 737.description: A three-week rotation in veterinary anesthesiology utilizing patients presented to the veterinary teaching hospital.

VMC 739.subject: VMC
VMC 739.description: Introduction of ethics in veterinary medicine, with specific attention to ethical theories, ethical decision making, moral status of animals, professional ethics, and practice issues.

VMC 740.subject: VMC
VMC 740.course_name: SHEEP AND GOAT MEDICINE AND SURGERY
VMC 740.description: Discussions of economically important sheep and goat diseases, practical surgeries, and a review of nutrition and husbandry.

VMC 741.subject: VMC
VMC 741.course_name: CLINICAL SKILLS VI: SMALL ANIMAL SURGERY AND ANESTHESIA
VMC 741.description: Synthesizes skills learned in small animal internal medicine, anesthesia and surgery courses to safely anesthetize and sterilize cats and dogs. Emphasizes sterile technique, surgical skills, medical record keeping and patient care while building client communication skills (written and verbal) as well as interdisciplinary veterinary team skills.

VMC 742.subject: VMC
VMC 742.description: Provides an in-depth introduction to camelid health care.

VMC 744.subject: VMC
VMC 744.description: Application of anatomy, lameness examination, nerve and joint anesthesia, diagnostic radiology, ultrasound and nuclear scintigraphy to diagnosis of lameness in horses.

VMC 745.subject: VMC
VMC 745.description: A course in basic personal and business finances, career skills, and legal aspects of veterinary practice. Graded P/N.

VMC 746.subject: VMC
VMC 746.description: Emphasizes clinical rotation at Veterinary Teaching Hospital (VTH) and explores pharmacy applications in practice (i.e. counseling, medication reconciliation, hazardous drug handling, drug information questions and responses, etc.). Delves into hands-on pharmacy practice including, but not limited to, regulatory aspects, prescription writing and processing, controlled substance compliance, unique challenges, drug compounding, general pharmacokinetics on commonly used VTH medications, pharmacy calculations, and practical applications.

VMC 747.subject: VMC
VMC 747.description: An additional two-week clinical rotation in veterinary anesthesiology utilizing patients presented to the Veterinary Teaching Hospital. Graded P/N.

VMC 748.subject: VMC
VMC 748.description: Utilizing modern, motorized equipment, cadaver specimens, and live hospital and client horses, students will learn and perform modern methods of equine dental prophylaxis and treatment.

VMC 749.subject: VMC
VMC 749.description: Advanced clinical course for 4th-year veterinary students in which they will assume additional responsibility for performing common radiographic procedures. Graded P/N.

VMC 750.subject: VMC
VMC 750.description: A one-week course for veterinary students focusing on equine nutrition that can be used in veterinary practice. Graded P/N.

VMC 751.subject: VMC
VMC 751.description: An advanced course in clinical ruminant nutrition dealing with nutritional problems of ruminants that might be encountered by a practicing veterinarian. Graded P/N.

VMC 752.subject: VMC
VMC 752.description: Additional clinical medicine training. Graded P/N.

VMC 753.subject: VMC
VMC 753.description: Teaches students a realistic approach to the diagnosis and treatment of pets with cancer. Students will participate in rounds, case management and medical records keeping.

VMC 754.subject: VMC
VMC 754.description: Additional clinical surgery training. Graded P/N.

VMC 755.subject: VMC
VMC 755.description: One additional rural practice training. Graded P/N.

VMC 756.subject: VMC
VMC 756.course_name: CLINICAL SKILLS V: TECHNICAL SKILLS AND CLINICAL REASONING
VMC 756.description: Development of technical and psychomotor skills and clinical reasoning in preparation for clinical coursework.

VMC 758.subject: VMC
VMC 758.description: Clinical application of production medicine practices to dairy and beef cattle practice.

VMC 759.subject: VMC
VMC 759.description: A laboratory for additional experience in rectal palpation of large animals, for third-year veterinary students. Graded P/N.

VMC 760.subject: VMC
VMC 760.course_name: CLINICAL SKILLS I: INTRO TO ANIMAL CARE AND VETERINARY MED
VMC 760.description: Introduction of a variety of topics relevant to veterinary clinical skills including professionalism, inclusion, ethics, and career options, In addition, animal care, handling, restraint, and physical exam skills will begin to be developed.

VMC 761.subject: VMC
VMC 761.course_name: CLINICAL SKILLS II: PHYSICAL EXAM AND PROBLEM SOLVING SKILLS
VMC 761.description: Introduction to problem solving and integration of clinical case and basic science in the veterinary curriculum. Development of physical exam skills on healthy animals and medical records keeping.

VMC 762.subject: VMC
VMC 762.course_name: CLINICAL SKILLS III: REASONING AND COMMUNICATION
VMC 762.description: Develop communication skills and clinical reasoning in preparation for client interactions and evidence-based decision-making.

VMC 763.subject: VMC
VMC 763.description: An elective course for junior veterinary students detailing diagnosis and management of the common congenital and acquired cardiac diseases of domestic animals.

VMC 764.subject: VMC
VMC 764.description: A lecture and laboratory course in diagnostic imaging covering physics or radiography and ultrasonography, radiation safety and image interpretation for small and large animals, presented by body systems.

VMC 765.subject: VMC
VMC 765.description: An elective advanced radiology case-based course for Year 3 veterinary medicine students that focuses on radiographic findings of commonly encountered clinical disease.

VMC 766.subject: VMC
VMC 766.description: A 1-week overview of clinical small animal ultrasonography with particular emphasis on material relevant to a general or emergency practitioner. Students will be able to perform a FAST scan to identify peritoneal fluid. Students will listen to didactic lectures in the morning with practical sessions in the afternoon. At the end of the week, pairs of students will make a short presentation based on a literature search on a topic of interest.

VMC 767.subject: VMC
VMC 767.description: Introductory course to provides instruction in veterinary ultrasound with an emphasis on image optimization, evaluation of the abdomen, description and interpretation of imaging findings in dogs and cats. This course is intended for students with a background in common small animal disease and imaging anatomy.

VMC 768.subject: VMC
VMC 768.description: A basic course in the principles and techniques of surgery and anesthesia for the professional veterinary student. Lec/lab.

VMC 769.subject: VMC
VMC 769.description: An introduction to medicine with a discussion of the principles of medicine that would be applicable to all species. Physical examination, clinical diagnosis, pathophysiology of signs of disease in domestic animals, therapeutic principles and diagnostic procedures.

VMC 770.subject: VMC
VMC 770.description: The first of three courses in large animal medicine for third-year professional veterinary students covering diagnosis and treatment of domestic large animals.

VMC 771.subject: VMC
VMC 771.description: Diagnosis, treatment and control of diseases of large domestic animals, specifically gastrointestinal, hepatobiliary diseases, weight loss, and introduction to production medicine, and some swine diseases.

VMC 772.subject: VMC
VMC 772.description: Emphasizes diagnosis, treatment, and control of diseases of large, domestic animals, specifically: disorders of gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, nervous, and musculoskeletal systems & eyes, udder, skin, neonates.

VMC 773.subject: VMC
VMC 773.description: Laboratory experience for third-year veterinary students concurrent with the large and small animal medicine courses.

VMC 774.subject: VMC
VMC 774.description: Laboratory experience for third-year veterinary students concurrent with the large and small animal medicine courses.

VMC 775.subject: VMC
VMC 775.course_name: CLINICAL SMALL SPORTS MEDICINE AND REHABILITATION
VMC 775.description: Clinical training in small animal rehabilitation in the Veterinary Teaching Hospital.

VMC 776.subject: VMC
VMC 776.description: A course for veterinary students describing major topics of small animal internal medicine, using both a systems-based approach and a problem-based approach.

VMC 777.subject: VMC
VMC 777.description: A course for veterinary students describing major topics of small animal internal medicine, using both a systems-based approach and a problem-based approach.

VMC 778.subject: VMC
VMC 778.description: A course for veterinary students describing major topics of small animal internal medicine, using both a systems-based approach and a problem-based approach.

VMC 779.subject: VMC
VMC 779.description: Encompasses basic exercise physiology, sports-related injuries, injury rehabilitation, training and nutrition of equine athletes.

VMC 780.subject: VMC
VMC 780.description: Theory of practice of veterinary medicine in a non-university situation. Graded P/N.

VMC 781.subject: VMC
VMC 781.description: Seminars and case discussions on selected topics by students, staff, and others. Graded P/N.

VMC 782.subject: VMC
VMC 782.description: Practice and instruction in caring for critically ill patients in the Veterinary Teaching Hospital.

VMC 783.subject: VMC
VMC 783.description: To present the clinical applications of reproductive physiology, anatomy, embryology, pathology and microbiology in domesticated animals.

VMC 784.subject: VMC
VMC 784.description: Utilize Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance (MR) image acquisition including physics, artifacts, systematic approach to image interpretation, and common disease identification in both large and small animal species. Apply knowledge by evaluating CT and MR studies in conjunction with relevant literature. Analyze clinical imaging cases using outcomes, follow-up imaging, and surgical and histologic findings.

VMC 785.subject: VMC
VMC 785.description: Integrates knowledge from previous courses and elaborates on specific diagnosis, operative methods, and aftercare of common small animal surgical conditions. Emphasizes topics and depth with the goal of preparing students for general small animal practice including general surgery, surgical oncology, orthopedic surgery, ophthalmic surgery and neurosurgery.

VMC 786.subject: VMC
VMC 786.description: Diagnosis and treatment of feline, canine and equine problem behaviors including aggression, anxiety, house-soiling and compulsive behaviors.

VMC 787.subject: VMC
VMC 787.description: An introductory clinical experience for third-year veterinary students.

VMC 789.subject: VMC
VMC 789.description: Additional clinical training in primary care pet practice at a Banfield Pet Hospital. Graded P/N.

VMC 790.subject: VMC
VMC 790.description: One- to four-week periods. Section 1: Large Animal Clinical Experience/Topics (1-16). Section 2: Small Animal Clinical Experience/Topics (1-16). Section 3: Mixed Animal Clinical Experience/Topics (1-16). Section 4: Small Animal Private Practice (1-16). Section 5: Special Studies (1-16). Some sections graded P/N. Lec/lab.

VMC 791.subject: VMC
VMC 791.description: A clinical rotation in small animal internal medicine at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital. Emphasis will be placed on patient evaluation, diagnosis and treatment of diseases of dogs and cats.

VMC 792.subject: VMC
VMC 792.description: A two-week, three-credit clinical elective rotation in small animal internal medicine at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital. Emphasis will be placed on patient evaluation, diagnosis and treatment of diseases of dogs and cats.

VMC 793.subject: VMC
VMC 793.description: Clinical training in small animal surgery in the Veterinary Teaching Hospital.
VMC 793.prerequisites_raw: VMC 725 with C or better and VMC 785 [C]

VMC 794.subject: VMC
VMC 794.course_name: OHS SMALL ANIMAL PRIMARY CARE AND SURGERY
VMC 794.description: Two-week rotation at OHS to gain experience with an emphasis on surgery, medical case workup, exam room protocol and behavior basics.

VMC 795.subject: VMC
VMC 795.description: Elective rotation at Community Practice Hospital located at the Oregon Humane Society in Portland, Oregon. Emphasizes student experience as the primary clinician in small animal general medicine and develops clinical skills regarding patient wellness, outpatient services, and client communication by interactions with a diverse clientele.

VMC 796.subject: VMC
VMC 796.description: A clinical course for 4th-year veterinary students in which they will assume primary responsibility for performing common radiographic procedures.

VMC 797.subject: VMC
VMC 797.description: Focuses on small animal critical care in the intensive care unit at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital. Covers techniques of medicine and critical care of the dog and cat with a hands-on experience in managing hospitalized patients within the ICU. Develops skills in history taking, physical examination, constructing a problem list, acquiring diagnostic samples and interpreting the results, administering treatments and supportive care, and assimilating medical records.

VMC 798.subject: VMC
VMC 798.description: Clinical training in small animal surgery in the College of Veterinary Medicine, Lois B. Acheson Veterinary Teaching Hospital.

WGSS 110.subject: WGSS
WGSS 110.description: Introduces students to the critical analysis of mass media and representations of women, gender, sexuality, and race in popular culture. Explores the entertainment industry, advertising, music, the internet and technology through a variety of lenses including feminist, queer, film, and disability theories.
attributes: CFAH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities General; CPWC – Bacc Core

WGSS 110H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 110H.description: Introduces students to the critical analysis of mass media and representations of women, gender, sexuality, and race in popular culture. Explores the entertainment industry, advertising, music, the internet and technology through a variety of lenses including feminist, queer, film, and disability theories.
attributes: CFAH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities General; CPWC – Bacc Core
Western Culture; HNRS – Honors Course Designator

WGSS 111.subject: WGSS
WGSS 111.description: Introduction to feminist analysis through the examination of current events and their relation to gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, class, age, and ability. Topics vary from term to term and may include issues related to politics, social movements, education, the workplace, science and technology, the environment, globalization, arts and culture, and the media. May be repeated for credit when topic varies. (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 140.subject: WGSS
WGSS 140.course_name: AI THROUGH GENDER, RACE, AND JUSTICE
WGSS 140.description: Examines ongoing systemic inequality and potential harm to already marginalized people based on gender, race, socioeconomic status, age, sexual orientation, and ability in society by the use of AI. Introduces an analysis of consumption, environmental impacts, and algorithm development through anti-racist, decolonial, and justice frameworks toward transparency, cooperative, and consent-focused AI development by using multidisciplinary perspectives.

WGSS 199.subject: WGSS
WGSS 199.description: Special topics of contemporary relevance to research of women and gender role issues. For students who seek an elementary introduction to a specific realm of women, gender, and sexuality studies. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.

WGSS 223.subject: WGSS
WGSS 223.course_name: +*INTRODUCTION TO WOMEN, GENDER, AND SEXUALITY STUDIES
WGSS 223.description: Introduces women, gender, and sexuality studies. Focuses on the lives and status of women in society and explores ways institutions such as family, work, media, law and religion affect different groups of women. Explores issues of gender, race, class, age, sexual orientation, size and ability from multidisciplinary perspectives.
attributes: Difference/Power/Discrimination; LACS – Liberal Arts Social Core

WGSS 223H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 223H.course_name: +*INTRODUCTION TO WOMEN, GENDER, AND SEXUALITY STUDIES
WGSS 223H.description: Introduces women, gender, and sexuality studies. Focuses on the lives and status of women in society and explores ways institutions such as family, work, media, law and religion affect different groups of women. Explores issues of gender, race, class, age, sexual orientation, size and ability from multidisciplinary perspectives.
attributes: Difference/Power/Discrimination; HNRS – Honors Course Designator; LACS – Liberal Arts Social Core

WGSS 224.subject: WGSS
WGSS 224.description: Examines the way the questioning of traditional gender roles and their accompanying power structures can lead to change in women's personal and public lives. Explores women's heritage and contributions and focuses on issues of self-growth and social movements for change.
attributes: Social Processes & Institutions; LACS – Liberal Arts Social Core

WGSS 225.subject: WGSS
WGSS 225.description: Explores constructions of gender, race, class, sexuality, and nation in the animated films of Walt Disney; introduces concepts in film theory and criticism, and develops analyses of the politics of representation.

WGSS 225H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 225H.description: Explores constructions of gender, race, class, sexuality, and nation in the animated films of Walt Disney; introduces concepts in film theory and criticism, and develops analyses of the politics of representation.

WGSS 235.subject: WGSS
WGSS 235.description: Explores constructions and practices of gender in a transnational, multi-religious, and global framework by examining a wide variety of films about women around the world.
attributes: CFGH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities Global; CPCD – Bacc Core
Cultural Diversity; LACN – Liberal Arts Non-Western Core

WGSS 235H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 235H.description: Explores constructions and practices of gender in a transnational, multi-religious, and global framework by examining a wide variety of films about women around the world.
attributes: CFGH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities Global; CPCD – Bacc Core
Cultural Diversity; HNRS – Honors Course Designator; LACN – Liberal Arts Non-Western Core

WGSS 240.subject: WGSS
WGSS 240.description: Focuses on sport as a gendered and racialized institution. Drawing from cultural, psychosocial, and political perspectives students examine intersections of gender with race, sexual identity, social class, ability, age, and religion.

WGSS 240H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 240H.description: Focuses on sport as a gendered and racialized institution. Drawing from cultural, psychosocial, and political perspectives students examine intersections of gender with race, sexual identity, social class, ability, age, and religion.
attributes: Social Processes & Institutions; HNRS – Honors Course Designator

WGSS 262.subject: WGSS
WGSS 262.description: Centering itself on activism and scholarship, this course examines homophobia's and transphobia's relationship with racism, colonialism, sexism, ableism, classism and other forms of oppression. Introduces key concepts, histories, and political frameworks within Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer political movements. CROSSLISTED as QS 262 / WGSS 262 . (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 262H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 262H.description: Centering itself on activism and scholarship, this course examines homophobia's and transphobia's relationship with racism, colonialism, sexism, ableism, classism and other forms of oppression. Introduces key concepts, histories, and political frameworks within Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, and Queer political movements. CROSSLISTED as QS 262 / WGSS 262 . (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 270.subject: WGSS
WGSS 270.description: Addresses issues of domestic violence, rape, dating violence, as well as contemporary social debates about pornography and the media's impact on violence in society, which includes a global perspective. Focuses on individual and collective practices resisting gender violence.
attributes: Social Processes & Institutions; LACS – Liberal Arts Social Core

WGSS 275.subject: WGSS
WGSS 275.description: Explores concepts of structural inequality, difference, power, and discrimination through a critical survey of arts activism. Requires critical thinking about artwork and artists which address a number of social issues in the United States, including race, ethnicity, class, gender, sexuality, immigration, and Indigeneity. Emphasizes various practicing artists and academics with a focus on counter narratives, intersectionality, fluid and multiple identities and communities while also examining many genres of art activism and readings. Includes a strong focus on Indigeneity. CROSSLISTED as ES 275 / QS 275 / WGSS 275 .
attributes: CFAH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities General; CPDP – Bacc Core

WGSS 280.subject: WGSS
WGSS 280.description: Focuses on women's experiences throughout the world and examines women's issues and status cross-culturally.
attributes: CFGH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities Global; CPCD – Bacc Core
Cultural Diversity; LACN – Liberal Arts Non-Western Core

WGSS 280H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 280H.description: Focuses on women's experiences throughout the world and examines women's issues and status cross-culturally. (Bacc Core Course)
attributes: CFGH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities Global; CPCD – Bacc Core
Cultural Diversity; HNRS – Honors Course Designator

WGSS 295.subject: WGSS
WGSS 295.description: Examines feminist interpretations of the Bible and pays special attention to intersections of race, social class, sexual identity, and nation in biblical interpretation.

WGSS 299.subject: WGSS
WGSS 299.course_name: TOPICS IN WOMEN, GENDER, AND SEXUALITY STUDIES
WGSS 299.description: Current topics related to women, gender and sexuality. Description and analysis of different realms of knowledge about gender issues.

WGSS 312.subject: WGSS
WGSS 312.description: Engagement in a study abroad experience in Western Europe with an emphasis on transnational, queer, and critical race feminist analysis.

WGSS 319.subject: WGSS
WGSS 319.description: Examines traditional scientific methods through a feminist philosophy of science lens that incorporates critiques of the racialized and gendered origins of modern science. Introduces the breadth of feminist research methods associated with social justice research. CROSSLISTED as ES 319 / WGSS 319 .
WGSS 319.prerequisites_raw: WGSS 223 with D- or better or WGSS 223H with D- or better

WGSS 320.subject: WGSS
WGSS 320.description: Explores women's contributions and focuses in technology fields. Analyzes gendered nature of technology. Theory and practice of technologies. (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 321.subject: WGSS
WGSS 321.description: Examines the concept of Queer popular culture through film, music, TV, image, and other mediums. Seeks to disrupt dominant discourses around gender and sexuality by centralizing women of color feminisms and queer of color critiques to analyze popular representations of gender, sexuality, race, class, disability, and other social locations. CROSSLISTED as QS 321 / WGSS 321 . (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 340.subject: WGSS
WGSS 340.description: Analyzes the relationship between society and science by explaining technology and science as gendered practices and bodies of knowledge. Focuses on the ways the making of women and men affect the making of science and explores the roles of women in scientific pursuits. (SS) (Bacc Core Course)
attributes: Science/Technology/Society; LACS – Liberal Arts Social Core

WGSS 340H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 340H.description: Analyzes the relationship between society and science by explaining technology and science as gendered practices and bodies of knowledge. Focuses on the ways the making of women and men affect the making of science and explores the roles of women in scientific pursuits. (SS) (Bacc Core Course)
attributes: Science/Technology/Society; HNRS – Honors Course Designator; LACS – Liberal Arts Social Core

WGSS 350.subject: WGSS
WGSS 350.course_name: *POLITICS OF MOTHERHOOD IN A GLOBAL CONTEXT
WGSS 350.description: Introduces students to the politics of motherhood in global contexts, focusing on politics of transnational adoption; motherhood, surrogacy, and biotechnologies; effects of globalization on mothering across borders; mothering in the global welfare state; movements for reproductive justice; and transnational representations of motherhood.

WGSS 360.subject: WGSS
WGSS 360.course_name: *MEN AND MASCULINITIES IN A GLOBAL CONTEXT
WGSS 360.description: Students will become familiar with central topics in global masculinity studies, analyze texts in diverse media, develop original arguments, and engage with issues of masculinity and representation through written and creative work. (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 360H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 360H.course_name: *MEN AND MASCULINITIES IN A GLOBAL CONTEXT
WGSS 360H.description: Students will become familiar with central topics in global masculinity studies, analyze texts in diverse media, develop original arguments, and engage with issues of masculinity and representation through written and creative work. (Bacc Core Course)
attributes: Contemporary Global Issues; HNRS – Honors Course Designator

WGSS 362.subject: WGSS
WGSS 362.description: Engages the ethics and responsibilities involved in serving LGBTQ+ communities in fields such as education, health, law, and social services for those entering and/or continuing professions in fields that historically underserve LGBTQ+ people. Topics include LGBTQ+ youth; LGBTQ+ elders; issues affecting LGBTQ+ people across their lifespans; approaches to cultural competency; violence against LGBTQ+ people, forms of oppression including heterosexism, homophobia, and transphobia; and LGBTQ+ community resilience. CROSSLISTED as QS 362 / WGSS 362 . (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 364.subject: WGSS
WGSS 364.description: Addresses transgender politics--including non-binary and gender non-conforming issues--through feminist and intersectional approaches by analyzing transgender theories, arts, and activism. CROSSLISTED as QS 364 / WGSS 364 .

WGSS 364H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 364H.description: Addresses transgender politics--including non-binary and gender non-conforming issues--through feminist and intersectional approaches by analyzing transgender theories, arts, and activism. CROSSLISTED as QS 364 / WGSS 364 .

WGSS 378.subject: WGSS
WGSS 378.description: Introduces students to the academic study of religion, as well as the academic study of gender. In order to offer a global perspective, we will read a series of case studies that deal with the religion as a gendered experience. Students will produce two essays, one of which will be based on independent research. CROSSLISTED as HST 378 / REL 378 / WGSS 378 .

WGSS 380.subject: WGSS
WGSS 380.description: Examines the lives and experiences of Muslim women in Islamic communities around the world from a variety of perspectives in order to highlight issues significant for contemporary Muslim women: family, education, work, politics, health, marriage, divorce, war, and violence.

WGSS 399.subject: WGSS
WGSS 399.course_name: TOPICS IN WOMEN, GENDER, AND SEXUALITY STUDIES
WGSS 399.description: Current topics in women, gender, and sexuality. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.

WGSS 399H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 399H.course_name: TOPICS IN WOMEN, GENDER, AND SEXUALITY STUDIES
WGSS 399H.description: Current topics in women, gender, and sexuality. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.

WGSS 410.subject: WGSS
WGSS 410.description: The internship experience provides the opportunity to gain experience within an off-campus private, public, or community agency or organization which has as one of its goals the improvement of the status of women in society. Students work with an on-site mentor who guides their field experience in collaboration with the internship coordinator in the WGSS program. Only 6 credits will count toward the Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies major.

WGSS 414.subject: WGSS
WGSS 414.description: Explores the ways different systems of oppression and discrimination impact women's lives. Examines sexism, classism, racism, and anti-Jewish oppression, as well as discrimination against queer women, older women, and those who differ in ability and appearance.
attributes: Difference/Power/Discrimination; CSDP – Core Ed - Advanced Difference
Power & Oppression; LACS – Liberal Arts Social Core
WGSS 414.prerequisites_raw: WGSS 223 with D- or better or WGSS 223H with D- or better

WGSS 416.subject: WGSS
WGSS 416.description: Explores feminist conceptions about the nature of the world, women's reality and visions for change. Analyzes major issues raised by the women's movement and the development of feminist ideas, as well as provides a critical examination of feminist thought and different theories which comprise it.
WGSS 416.prerequisites_raw: WS 223 with D- or better or WS 223H with D- or better or WS 224 with D- or better or WGSS 223 with D- or better or WGSS 223H with D- or better or WGSS 224 with D- or better

WGSS 430.subject: WGSS
WGSS 430.description: Explores the contemporary experiences of women of color, as well as the theoretical and practical frameworks of women of color feminisms. Analyses key themes in women of color feminisms, including politics of representation, multiple forms of state and interpersonal violence, intersecting forms of oppression, economic justice, reproductive justice, and strategies of resistance.
WGSS 430.prerequisites_raw: WS 223 with D- or better or WS 223H with D- or better or WGSS 223 with D- or better or WGSS 223H with D- or better

WGSS 431.subject: WGSS
WGSS 431.description: "Queer of color critiques" refers to political theories and activism that emerge from LGBTQ people of color to examine the intersections between race, sexuality and gender. Addresses these intersections through theory, history, and activism. CROSSLISTED as ES 431 / QS 431 / WGSS 431 and ES 531 / QS 531 / WGSS 531 .

WGSS 432.subject: WGSS
WGSS 432.description: A creative and discussion-based course focusing on ways in which photography can and has addressed issues of gender and sexuality. An introduction to key concepts and intersections in Women's, Gender and Sexuality Studies; Queer Studies and photography theory. Create written and photographic responses to artworks, texts, personal experience and pop-culture. CROSSLISTED as ART 432 / QS 432 / WGSS 432 and ART 532 / QS 532 .

WGSS 440.subject: WGSS
WGSS 440.description: Explores the relationship between women and natural resources. In particular, the course examines the roles of policy, technology, culture, and management in women's use and control of natural resources. (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 440H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 440H.description: Explores the relationship between women and natural resources. In particular, the course examines the roles of policy, technology, culture, and management in women's use and control of natural resources. (Bacc Core Course)

WGSS 449.subject: WGSS
WGSS 449.description: Explores Indigenous feminisms as well as some of the issues facing Indigenous women in the Americas and Pacific Islands. Relates Indigenous feminisms to the complexity of federal law and policies as well as land struggles between Indigenous communities and contemporary settler colonial nations. Raises awareness of current Indigenous struggles as well as Indigenous feminist responses and resistance to these same struggles. CROSSLISTED as ES 449 / QS 449 / WGSS 449 .
WGSS 449.recommended: Critical thinking, evaluation, and synthesis skills

WGSS 460.subject: WGSS
WGSS 460.description: Explores the historical, theoretical, and political dimensions of female sexuality. Examines the basic assumptions about the meaning of gendered sexuality, how it has been shaped and controlled, and why women's sexuality has been/is a source of both women's liberation and subjugation. Incorporates Queer and Trans* theories about gendered/women's sexualities.
attributes: CSWC – Core Ed - Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); CWIC – Bacc Core
Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); LACS – Liberal Arts Social Core
WGSS 460.prerequisites_raw: WGSS 223 with D- or better or WGSS 223H with D- or better or WGSS 224 with D- or better

WGSS 462.subject: WGSS
WGSS 462.description: Engages key themes and critical frameworks in queer theories. Topics include histories of sexuality; forms of oppression, including heterosexism, homophobia, and transphobia; resistance to oppression; violence against LGBTQ people; queer activism; diverse experiences of sexuality; and representations in literature, art, and popular media. CROSSLISTED as QS 462 / WGSS 462 and QS 562 / WGSS 562 .

WGSS 472.subject: WGSS
WGSS 472.description: "Two-spirit" refers to North American indigenous genders outside of European male/female binaries. Two-spirit communities argue for decolonization as a central political struggle, calling all people to unlearn settler colonial gender/sexuality on Native land. Addresses indigenous two-spirit/GLBTQ issues through theory, literature, activism, and art. CROSSLISTED as QS 472 / WGSS 472 .
attributes: CSWC – Core Ed - Writing Intensive Curriculum (WIC); CWIC – Bacc Core

WGSS 473.subject: WGSS
WGSS 473.description: With a particular focus on transgender people of color and transnational constructions of gender, engages issues in the lives of Transgender people through autobiography, memoir, biography, poetry, and documentary film. CROSSLISTED as QS 473 / WGSS 473 and QS 573 / WGSS 573 .

WGSS 475.subject: WGSS
WGSS 475.course_name: *RACE, GENDER, AND LABOR ON THE OREGON COAST
WGSS 475.description: Examines the sociopolitical and cultural processes that constitute coastal spaces in Oregon, including issues of race/ethnicity, immigration, labor/class, and gender, as these shape and are shaped by human interactions with the coast and the ocean. In addition to reading, writing, and discussion, engage in guided-inquiry and problem-solving projects, to explore substantive issues in Newport and other locations along the Oregon coast. Takes advantage of the Hatfield Marine Science Center and available technologies, to connect students with Newport and other coastal locations including Coos Bay, Lincoln City, and Astoria. CROSSLISTED as ES 475 / WGSS 475 .
WGSS 475.recommended: Junior class standing; collaboration, critical thinking, and synthesis skills

WGSS 476.subject: WGSS
WGSS 476.description: Explores contemporary experiences of sexualities within transnational contexts. Analyzes themes including queer and LGBTQI organizing, same-sex desires, queer transnational immigration and labor flows, sex industries and discourses of trafficking, sex tourism, and reproductive justice, using feminist, queer, and postcolonial theoretical frameworks. CROSSLISTED as QS 476 / WGSS 476 and QS 576 / WGSS 576 .
WGSS 476.prerequisites_raw: QS 262 with D- or better or QS 262H with D- or better or WGSS 262 with D- or better or WGSS 262H with D- or better

WGSS 477.subject: WGSS
WGSS 477.course_name: QUEER/TRANS PEOPLE OF COLOR ARTS AND ACTIVISM
WGSS 477.description: LGBTQ people of color often engage struggles for social justice through artistic movements. Focuses on arts by LGBTQ people of color and the way these artistic movements contribute to activism that interrupts interlocking systems of oppression. CROSSLISTED as ES 477 / QS 477 / WGSS 477 and ES 577/ QS 577 / WGSS 577 .

WGSS 480.subject: WGSS
WGSS 480.description: Focuses on social constructions of gender in global context. Explores the comparative realities of various gendered struggles for social justice and studies key definitions and theoretical assumptions relevant to the subject of global feminist activism.
attributes: Contemporary Global Issues; LACN – Liberal Arts Non-Western Core
WGSS 480.prerequisites_raw: WGSS 223 with D- or better or WGSS 223H with D- or better or WGSS 224 with D- or better

WGSS 480H.subject: WGSS
WGSS 480H.description: Focuses on social constructions of gender in global context. Explores the comparative realities of various gendered struggles for social justice and studies key definitions and theoretical assumptions relevant to the subject of global feminist activism.
attributes: Contemporary Global Issues; HNRS – Honors Course Designator; LACN – Liberal Arts Non-Western Core
WGSS 480H.prerequisites_raw: WGSS 223 with D- or better or WGSS 223H with D- or better or WGSS 224 with D- or better

WGSS 482.subject: WGSS
WGSS 482.description: Women's health issues are examined from a global perspective in the context of a woman's life and through a feminist political lens. Central to our discussions will be an analysis of the interplay among race, class, and gender in shaping particular health care outcomes. The course stresses the potential for women's agency and autonomy with respect to improving their health and environments.

WGSS 483.subject: WGSS
WGSS 483.description: Based on a social justice framework, explores the intersections of race, gender, ethnicity, disability and sexuality to provide a deeper understanding of how these factors shape health inequities in diverse communities nationally and globally.

WGSS 498.subject: WGSS
WGSS 498.description: Focuses on central questions for feminist research and activism. Develops deeper understandings of the process of generating feminist knowledge and its application in diverse forms of feminist practice.
attributes: CSC1 – Core Ed - Beyond OSU Career Preparation; CSC2 – Core Ed - Beyond OSU Career Engagement
WGSS 498.prerequisites_raw: WGSS 414 with D- or better and WGSS 416 [D-] and ( CORE 100 [D-] or CORE 300 [D-] or BA 100 [D-] or BA 300 [D-] or LA 100 [D-] or LA 300 [D-] or SCI 100 [D-] or SCI 300 [D-] or ED 100 [D-] or ED 300 [D-] or ENGR 110 [D-] or ENGR 110H [D-] or ENGR 310 [D-] or Baccalaureate Core Student with a score of 1)

WGSS 511.subject: WGSS
WGSS 511.description: The WGSS 511 , 512 , 513 sequence prepares Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies graduate students to succeed in their courses of study and in their chosen profession. WGSS 511 provides knowledge about Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies as a discipline and as a course of study that helps students manage the transition to graduate school.

WGSS 512.subject: WGSS
WGSS 512.description: The WGSS 511 , 512 , 513 sequence prepares Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies graduate students to succeed in their courses of study and in their chosen profession. WGSS 512 guides students in the development of an intellectual life with a focus on thriving and surviving as a scholar in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies.

WGSS 513.subject: WGSS
WGSS 513.description: The WGSS 511 , 512 , 513 sequence prepares Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies graduate students to succeed in their courses of study and in their chosen profession. WGSS 513 focuses on helping students shape a future that utilizes the graduate degree in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies. It helps students manage the transition to life after the Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies Master's program at OSU.

WGSS 514.subject: WGSS
WGSS 514.course_name: SYSTEMS OF OPPRESSION: STRATEGIES FOR RESISTANCE
WGSS 514.description: Explores the ways different systems of oppression function in society. Applies feminist intersectionality approaches to examine interlocking systems of inequality and privilege.

WGSS 516.subject: WGSS
WGSS 516.description: Explores feminist conceptions about the nature of the world, women's reality and visions for change. Analyzes major issues raised by the women's movement and the development of feminist ideas, as well as provides a critical examination of feminist thought and different theories which comprise it.
WGSS 516.recommended: WS 223 or WS 223H or WS 224 or WGSS 223 or WGSS 223H or WGSS 224

WGSS 518.subject: WGSS
WGSS 518.description: Explores the socio-political and historical context out of which traditional research methodologies emerge and the relationship of gender to scientific pursuits. Teaches what it means to do emancipatory anti-sexist and participatory research.

WGSS 521.subject: WGSS
WGSS 521.description: Examines theories of feminist leadership and applications in non-profit, governmental, and higher education institutions.

WGSS 524.subject: WGSS
WGSS 524.description: Addresses transgender politics--including transsexual, genderqueer, and gender non-conforming issues--through feminist and intersectional approaches by analyzing transgender theories, arts, and activism. CROSSLISTED as QS 524 / WGSS 524 .

WGSS 530.subject: WGSS
WGSS 530.description: Explores the contemporary experiences of women of color, as well as the theoretical and practical frameworks of women of color feminisms. Analyses key themes in women of color feminisms, including politics of representation, multiple forms of state and interpersonal violence, intersecting forms of oppression, economic justice, reproductive justice, and strategies of resistance.
WGSS 530.recommended: WGSS 223 or WGSS 223H or WS 223 or WS 223H

WGSS 531.subject: WGSS
WGSS 531.description: "Queer of color critiques" refers to political theories and activism that emerge from LGBTQ people of color to examine the intersections between race, sexuality and gender. Addresses these intersections through theory, history, and activism. CROSSLISTED as ES 431 / QS 431 / WGSS 431 and ES 531 / QS 531 / WGSS 531 .

WGSS 535.subject: WGSS
WGSS 535.description: Focuses on the experiences and practices of the feminist classroom. Key components of the class include issues associated with the identity and development of the teacher, as well as the development of skills to help facilitate understanding, empowerment, and the personal and social agency of students.

WGSS 549.subject: WGSS
WGSS 549.description: Explores Indigenous feminisms as well as some of the issues facing Indigenous women in the Americas and Pacific Islands. Relates Indigenous feminisms to the complexity of federal law and policies as well as land struggles between Indigenous communities and contemporary settler colonial nations. Raises awareness of current Indigenous struggles as well as Indigenous feminist responses and resistance to these same struggles. CROSSLISTED as ES 549 / QS 549 / WGSS 549 .

WGSS 555.subject: WGSS
WGSS 555.description: Graduate students are introduced to current methods and modes of feminist literary, visual culture, performance, new media, and film studies with a focus on application. In doing so, the course focuses on feminist approaches to key topics within textual studies (such as form, authors, and readers) as well as distinct methodological approaches to various genres and mediums (including poems, performances, photographs, and films).

WGSS 562.subject: WGSS
WGSS 562.description: Engages key themes and critical frameworks in queer theories. Topics include histories of sexuality; forms of oppression, including heterosexism, homophobia, and transphobia; resistance to oppression; violence against LGBTQ people; queer activism; diverse experiences of sexuality; and representations in literature, art, and popular media. CROSSLISTED as QS 462 / WGSS 462 and QS 562 / WGSS 562 .

WGSS 572.subject: WGSS
WGSS 572.description: "Two-spirit" refers to North American indigenous genders outside of European male/female binaries. Two-spirit communities argue for decolonization as a central political struggle, calling all people to unlearn settler colonial gender/sexuality on Native land. Addresses indigenous two-spirit/GLBTQ issues through theory, literature, activism, and art. CROSSLISTED as QS 472 / WGSS 472 and QS 572 / WGSS 572 .

WGSS 573.subject: WGSS
WGSS 573.description: With a particular focus on transgender people of color and transnational constructions of gender, engages issues in the lives of Transgender people through autobiography, memoir, biography, poetry, and documentary film. CROSSLISTED as QS 473 / WGSS 473 and QS 573 / WGSS 573 .

WGSS 575.subject: WGSS
WGSS 575.course_name: CRITICAL RACE FEMINISM AND OUTSIDER JURISPRUDENCE
WGSS 575.description: Critical exploration of critical legal justice movements and their relationship to social identities. Seminar emphasizes specific legal cases, federal and state laws, and constitutional issues that impact groups deemed outsiders in legal discourse as well as their social implications. The critical justice movement and anti-subordination struggles will be explored via case analyses that shape race, class, gender, sexuality, and disability relations. Theoretical contributions of law and society, critical race theory, LatCrit, and critical race feminism, critical white studies, critical mixed race studies, OutCrit, ClassCrit, and critical disability studies applied to historical precedent and current attempts at marginalizing/empowering communities. CROSSLISTED as ES 575 / WGSS 575 .

WGSS 576.subject: WGSS
WGSS 576.description: Explores contemporary experiences of sexualities within transnational contexts. Analyzes themes including queer and LGBTQI organizing, same-sex desires, queer transnational immigration and labor flows, sex industries and discourses of trafficking, sex tourism, and reproductive justice, using feminist, queer, and postcolonial theoretical frameworks. CROSSLISTED as QS 476 / WGSS 476 and QS 576 / WGSS 576 .

WGSS 577.subject: WGSS
WGSS 577.course_name: QUEER/TRANS PEOPLE OF COLOR ARTS AND ACTIVISM
WGSS 577.description: LGBTQ people of color often engage struggles for social justice through artistic movements. Focuses on arts by LGBTQ people of color and the way these artistic movements contribute to activism that interrupts interlocking systems of oppression. CROSSLISTED as QS 577 / WGSS 577 .

WGSS 582.subject: WGSS
WGSS 582.description: Women's health issues are examined from a global perspective in the context of a woman's life and through a feminist political lens. Central to our discussions will be an analysis of the interplay among race, class, and gender in shaping particular health care outcomes. The course stresses the potential for women's agency and autonomy with respect to improving their health and environments.

WGSS 583.subject: WGSS
WGSS 583.description: Based on a social justice framework, explores the intersections of race, gender, ethnicity, disability and sexuality to provide a deeper understanding of how these factors shape health inequities in diverse communities nationally and globally.

WGSS 585.subject: WGSS
WGSS 585.description: Introduces students to themes and theoretical principles of transnational feminisms, with special emphasis placed on feminist movements of the global South. We will explore colonialism, globalization, nation-building, representation, global economies, militarism, human rights, and politics of gender, race, class, sexuality, and nation.

WGSS 586.subject: WGSS
WGSS 586.description: Prepares students to participate in a short-term study abroad experience that emphasizes volunteer experiences in women's organizations and analysis from transnational feminist perspectives.

WGSS 587.subject: WGSS
WGSS 587.description: Engages students in a short-term study abroad experience that emphasizes volunteer experiences in women's organizations and analysis from transnational feminist perspectives.
WGSS 587.recommended: WS 486 or WS 586 or WGSS 486 or WGSS 586

WGSS 588.subject: WGSS
WGSS 588.description: Students reflect on their short-term study abroad experience by engaging in in-depth transnational feminist analysis of particular aspects of the study abroad experience.
WGSS 588.recommended: (WS 586 and WS 587) or ( WGSS 586 and WGSS 587 )

WGSS 599.subject: WGSS
WGSS 599.description: Topics on contemporary research in women, gender, and sexuality. May be repeated for credit when topic varies.

WGSS 601.subject: WGSS
WGSS 601.description: Individual and collaborative research and scholarship under the supervision of faculty.

WGSS 602.subject: WGSS
WGSS 602.description: Independent study in some field of special interest under the supervision of a faculty member.

WGSS 605.subject: WGSS
WGSS 605.description: Independent reading in specialized topics, guided by discussions in conference with faculty.

WGSS 606.subject: WGSS
WGSS 606.description: Special project initiation and participation under the supervision of faculty.

WGSS 610.subject: WGSS
WGSS 610.description: The internship experience provides opportunities to gain experience in a private, public, or community agency or organization, which has social justice advocacy as one of its goals. Students work with an on-site mentor who guides their field experience in collaboration with the internship coordinator in the WGSS program. One feature of graduate internships is the opportunity to shadow key personnel in order to meet internship goals.

WGSS 611.subject: WGSS
WGSS 611.description: Provides presentations of feminist research by OSU faculty and graduate students and faculty members from other institutions.

WGSS 616.subject: WGSS
WGSS 616.course_name: MULTIRACIAL, TRANSNATIONAL, AND QUEER FEMINISMS I
WGSS 616.description: Introduces doctoral students to foundational and emerging themes and texts in women, gender, and sexuality studies, with particular emphases on women of color feminisms, transnational feminisms, and queer feminist critiques. The first seminar in a two-part sequence ( WGSS 616 and 617 ).

WGSS 617.subject: WGSS
WGSS 617.course_name: MULTIRACIAL, TRANSNATIONAL, AND QUEER FEMINISMS II
WGSS 617.description: Introduces doctoral students to foundational and emerging themes and texts in women, gender, and sexuality studies, with particular emphases on women of color feminisms, transnational feminisms, and queer feminist critiques. The second seminar in a two-part sequence ( WGSS 616 and 617 ).

WGSS 619.subject: WGSS
WGSS 619.description: Navigates from feminist philosophy of science interventions to postcolonial, Chicana/Latina, and critical race criticisms of methodological stances in "normal" science. Standpoint methodologies, racialized and gendered origins of modern statistical methods, longstanding affinity between colonial inequalities and Eurocentric scientific inquiry, and successor sciences/sciences from below constitute the main themes of the course.

WGSS 620.subject: WGSS
WGSS 620.description: An examination of social justice theories and practices. Specifically engages with issues of power and privilege, systems of oppression, intersectionality, and social activism. Explores the practices of social justice movements.

WLC 159.subject: WLC
WLC 159.course_name: *LANGUAGE, RACE AND RACISM IN THE US: AN INTRODUCTION
WLC 159.description: Unpack language, race and racism--as well as the intersections between those ideas-- as cornerstones to understanding identity and society as inherently socially constructed notions. CROSSLISTED as ANTH 159 / ES 159 / WLC 159 . (Bacc Core Course)

WLC 220.subject: WLC
WLC 220.course_name: +*FRANCOPHONE CULTURES IN FILM: COLONIAL WARS AND INDEPENDENCE MOVEMENTS IN FRANCOPHONE FILMS
WLC 220.description: Explores the diverse cultures within the Francophone world through the lens of cinema. Includes engaging films that depict the socio-historical, political, economic, and cultural contexts of French-speaking regions, focusing particularly on the themes of colonialism, decolonization, and post-colonialism. Examines various regions, including North and Sub-Saharan Africa, and Vietnam, providing a comprehensive understanding of the impact of colonial and independence movements. Taught in English.
attributes: CFGH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities Global; CPCD – Bacc Core

WLC 230.subject: WLC
WLC 230.course_name: *FRANCE TODAY: CULTURES WITHIN AND BEYOND ITS BORDERS
WLC 230.description: An exploratory study of French culture and society since 1945. Topics include: decolonization, immigration, Francophone intellectual currents, France's European vocation, and social conflict today. Conducted in English.

WLC 231.subject: WLC
WLC 231.description: Explores the cultures of Germany’s 20th-century dictatorships: National Socialism or Nazism (1933-45) and East German Socialism (1949-89). Analyzes various primary sources with an emphasis on visual media (e.g., art and architecture, cinema, and graphic novels). Examines political, historical, ideological, and aesthetic aspects of the two regimes through various secondary sources with emphases on body politics (e.g., race/ethnicity, gender, ability, etc.)
attributes: CFAH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities General; CPWC – Bacc Core

WLC 231H.subject: WLC

WLC 232.subject: WLC
WLC 232.description: Provides a survey of the development of Chinese culture from prehistoric times to the end of the 19th century. Analyzes the teachings of major Chinese philosophies and religions. Describes the Chinese language and the evolution of its writing system. Examines the achievements in literature and the arts, science, and technology. Explains Chinese social and political institutions. Discusses trades and cultural interactions with other countries. Taught in English.
attributes: CFGH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities Global; CPCD – Bacc Core
Cultural Diversity; LACH – Liberal Arts Humanities Core; LACN – Liberal Arts Non-Western Core

WLC 233.subject: WLC
WLC 233.description: Examines the conditions of Chinese society and culture from the early 20th century to the present with emphasis on reform, revolution, political movements, and cultural transformation. Analyzes the domestic and global impacts of China's economic reform and the ongoing democracy movement and the prospect of China’s political reform. Discusses mainland China’s relationships with Hong Kong and Taiwan and the future of China's reunification. Taught in English.
attributes: CFGH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities Global; CPCD – Bacc Core
Cultural Diversity; LACH – Liberal Arts Humanities Core; LACN – Liberal Arts Non-Western Core

WLC 235.subject: WLC
WLC 235.description: Explores an introductory survey of Japanese history, mythology, folktales, poetry, arts, literature, society, theaters, the Tea ceremony, Ikebana, Japanese gardens, and traditions from ancient times to the mid-16th century. Taught in English.

Cultural Diversity; LACN – Liberal Arts Non-Western Core

attributes: CFGH – Core Ed - Art & Humanities Global; CPCD – Bacc Core

WLC 334.subject: WLC
WLC 334.course_name: FASHION AND DESIGN IN THE FRANCOPHONE WORLD
WLC 334.description: A study of the world of French fashion and design: origins and history, what's new and exciting in French fashion today and attitudes about fashion and beauty of design that have given the French the inside track on prestige in this arena for centuries.

WR 220.subject: WR

Students will complete readings, watch videos, participate in discussions, and demonstrate understanding through weekly quizzes. They will also challenge themselves with numerous writing activities, and complete writing analysis projects. (Bacc Core Course)
